Sixty-three central banks own it: its capital is held by central banks only, private shares having been bought back in 2001, and the owners run from the Federal Reserve System, the Bank of England, the Bank of France, the Deutsche Bundesbank and the European Central Bank to the People's Bank of China, the Bank of Japan, the Bank of Russia, the Reserve Bank of India, the Saudi Central Bank, the South African Reserve Bank and the Reserve Bank of Australia. It also runs money for five of them, and holds gold for eight, which is custody rather than management. On the management side it manages investment pools that central banks buy units in: the BCEAO holds units in its BISIP K fund, Slovakia's renminbi investment sits in its BISIP CNY, a small part of New Zealand's reserves is in its Asian Bond Fund, Chinese Yuan Bond Fund and US Dollar Green Bond Fund, Colombia holds units in two of its pools, and Timor-Leste's Petroleum Fund uses it as one of its outside managers. It also holds gold for several central banks, which is custody rather than management. The Reserve Bank of India keeps part of India's gold in safe custody with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements. The Bank of Portugal has 641,030 fine ounces there, about 5 per cent of its total. The National Bank of Belgium says a much smaller portion of its gold is held at the Bank for International Settlements and the Bank of Canada. The Bank of Japan's gold claims were moved, by a notice dating from 2000, out of a sight account and into an ear-marked account, meaning gold held for the depositor; the change was technical, with no new gold bought. The governor of Argentina's central bank, Santiago Bausili, told the Senate that part of its gold is deposited at the Bank for International Settlements in Switzerland, without attaching a tonnage to the location. The Central Bank of West African States keeps gold there as well, alongside its own head office and the Banque de France, put by Agence Ecofin at close to 106,000 ounces valued at 176.4 billion CFA francs and falling during 2024 as part of the gold was redeployed into placement operations; it has also bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, managed by the Bank for International Settlements, worth 205,811 million CFA francs on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million a year earlier. The Banco Central del Ecuador keeps 774,962.772 troy ounces with it at 31 December 2025, the bulk of the 844,962.772 ounces it holds abroad, the rest sitting with Citibank. The Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée holds 7,104.923 ounces there, a small part of a stock whose larger portions sit with three commercial handlers. The Banco Central de Timor-Leste names it as one of six firms running mandates for the Petroleum Fund, Timor-Leste's oil savings fund, as at 30 June 2025. One record is a career: Joachim Nagel, a Deutsche Bundesbank Executive Board member from 2010 to 2016 and its President since January 2022, moved to the KfW Executive Board and then to the Bank for International Settlements.
n:Merrill Lynch: Merrill Lynch, a bank in New York, employed an official of the Bank of Israel, Israel's central bank. Jacob Frenkel, Governor of the Bank of Israel 1991-2000, went from International Monetary Fund Economic Counselor to Bank of Israel Governor, then became chairman of Merrill Lynch International. Riad Salameh worked at the firm from 1973 to 1993, managing the personal portfolio of Rafic Hariri, who as prime minister appointed him governor of the Banque du Liban in 1993.
n:AIG: AIG, a company in New York, employed an official of the Bank of Israel, Israel's central bank. Jacob Frenkel, Governor of the Bank of Israel 1991-2000, went from International Monetary Fund Economic Counselor to Bank of Israel Governor, then to chairman of Merrill Lynch International and then vice-chairman of AIG.
n:JPMorgan Chase: JPMorgan Chase is a bank with its parent in New York, United States. It is the largest shareholder of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with 60,600,000 shares, or 29.5 per cent, as at 31 December 2018, down from 41.7 per cent in 2007, according to a 24 February 2020 article in Institutional Investor based on a freedom-of-information release of the New York Fed's capital stock records. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. Several central bankers have worked at the bank. Jacob Frenkel, a former Governor of the Bank of Israel, was chairman of JPMorgan Chase International, with no dates or order given. J. Aloysius Tarlue, Jr. was a compliance officer at J.P. Morgan Chase before becoming Executive Governor of the Central Bank of Liberia in 2020. Luis Caputo came from trading and country-head roles at JP Morgan and Deutsche Bank to head Argentina's central bank from June to 25 September 2018. Yaseen Anwar trained at JPMorgan Chase from 1973 to 1975 before a career that led to Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2007 and Governor in October 2011. n:Gallo Cambios: Gallo Cambios is an exchange house in Argentina. La Nación reported on 17 April 2026 that the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (BCRA) is examining a circuit that moved at least 900 million US dollars between January 2022 and October 2023. In it, dollars bought at the official rate allegedly ended up in the parallel market through exchange houses. The BCRA opened procedures against officials over its ethics rules, after raids at the bank that followed reports from the UIF and Procelac. The companies deny wrongdoing. The matter is unproven.

n:Financial Stability Board: The Financial Stability Board is a forum based in Basel, Switzerland, where central banks and other financial authorities take part. The central banks named include those of Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India and Indonesia. For each country the board lists the institutions that sit on it, usually the finance ministry and the central bank, and sometimes a market or banking regulator such as the Securities and Exchange Board of India or Germany's BaFin. Officials of these central banks take part in the board. The same central banks also belong to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).

n:PwC: PwC is an accounting firm based in London, United Kingdom, and it audits the accounts of eleven central banks and of the Bank for International Settlements, the bank for central banks. Its Finnish arm was recommended as auditor of the Bank of Finland on 7 October 2025 and approved by a Council decision of 13 November 2025 for the financial years 2026 to 2031, and its Portuguese arm was approved by a Council decision of 12 July 2022 for the Bank of Portugal for 2022 to 2026. At the Bank of Canada it audits jointly with Ernst & Young, with a report dated 26 February 2026 on the 2025 accounts. It signed the 2025 accounts of the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (report dated 30 April 2026), Danmarks Nationalbank (Copenhagen, 24 February 2026), the Central Bank of Brazil and the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the South African Reserve Bank's accounts for the year ended 31 March 2023 (report of 12 June 2023), the Saudi Central Bank's for the fiscal year ended 30 June 2023, and the National Bank of Rwanda's for the year ended 30 June 2022, in a report signed at Kigali on 12 October 2022. For the Bank for International Settlements it audited the year to 31 March 2026, the seventh and final year of its term, with a new auditor to be proposed. Sheila M'mbijjewe was a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers, as well as a director of Standard Chartered Bank and a non-executive director of Ecobank, before becoming Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya. The firm also appears in one case: a July 2013 report by the UN Monitoring Group for Somalia and Eritrea said 80 per cent of withdrawals from the Central Bank of Somalia were made for private purposes and that the governor was key to irregularities, with 12 million of 16.9 million US dollars transferred by PricewaterhouseCoopers untraceable. The central bank rejected the allegations.
n:BDO: BDO is an accounting firm based in Zaventem, Belgium. It audits five central banks. At the South African Reserve Bank it is one of two external auditors for 2025/26, together with Ernst & Young. At the State Bank of Pakistan its local firm, BDO Ebrahim & Co., audited the year ended 30 June 2026, with a report dated 27 August 2026. It audited the Banco de Mocambique for 2019, and an IMF Central Bank Transparency Code review of the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten states that BDO B.V. audited its 2024 financial statements.

n:Crane AB: Crane AB is a banknote printer based in Tumba, Sweden, tied to three central banks. It printed Swedish banknotes at Tumba, a plant it bought from Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, in 2002. On 19 June 2018 the Riksbank gave notice to end the contract because Crane was moving printing to Malta. In 2017 Brazil's central bank contracted it for 100 million notes of 2 reais, at a cost of 20.2 million reais. In Kenya, Crane challenged the central bank's award of a new currency printing tender to De La Rue as irregular and not transparent. The Central Bank of Kenya rejected those claims.
n:Oberthur Fiduciaire: Oberthur Fiduciaire is a banknote printer based in Paris, France, tied to 13 central banks, for which it prints or supplies notes. Danmarks Nationalbank chose it as its new banknote supplier under a four-year framework, with the first notes in circulation in 2020. In Germany it won a Deutsche Bundesbank tender to print part of the euro notes for 2013, after an earlier award about two years before that losing bidders had challenged without success; the Bundesbank's tender for 2012 gave it 526 million 10-euro notes. The Banco Central de Bolivia awarded it an international tender on 27 July 2023 worth 25,945,787 US dollars, for 321.5 million notes of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 bolivianos. The National Bank of Ethiopia gave it 19.6 million birr of a 206 million birr printing deal, covering the 50 birr note. In North Macedonia the national bank signed a contract, reported on 8 May 2026, to print 100-denar notes for 59,800,000 denars, about 972,358 euros; an earlier contract for the same note, reported in September 2021, had gone to the Russian firm Goznak for about 400,000 euros. The Bank of Uganda's director of currency told a parliamentary committee that the bank's banknote printing contract is with Oberthur, signed on 26 July 2018. The Central Bank of Costa Rica opened a tender in the second half of 2008 for six new denominations and Oberthur won it, printing the 20,000-colon note of 2010 at its plant in Rennes, France. The Bank of the Republic of Haiti ordered a reprint of 30 million 10-gourde notes for 845,000 euros. Single notes or part-series are also recorded in Mauritius (the 25 and 50 rupee notes), Tunisia (the 20-dinar note), Uruguay (the 2,000-peso note of 2015, introduced on 27 April 2016), Burundi (the 2,000-franc note of 11 September 2023) and Bosnia and Herzegovina, where every denomination except the 200 convertible mark note is reported to be printed by the firm.
n:Crane Currency: Crane Currency is a banknote printer based in Dalton, United States. A release from Curaçao says it is headquartered in Massachusetts, has plants in Malta and Sweden, and supplies more than 50 central banks. Twelve central banks are tied to it. It prints for Curaçao and Sint Maarten (the new Caribbean guilder), Liberia, Norway, where Norges Bank's own page on its banknote series says the printing has been carried out by Crane from 2020, Honduras, where La Prensa reported the Banco Central de Honduras awarding private tender 11/2023 to Crane Currency Malta, and Tanzania, where Crane Currency of Malta was one of two winners of a tender reported on 28 May 2024 to reprint the 10,000, 5,000, 2,000 and 1,000 shilling notes. It prints some of the notes of Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon and Mozambique, each recorded from a banknote-trade entry naming the printer on a single new denomination. It has supplied banknotes or related materials to Mexico, Guyana and Aruba. It has supplied banknote paper and security features to the US Treasury since 1879, though the customer there is the Treasury, not the Federal Reserve. In Liberia, Crane printed under two contracts totalling 15 billion Liberian dollars at a cost of US$15,331,689.20. A presidential investigation team alleged that Crane conspired with Central Bank of Liberia officials to print 18,151,000,000 Liberian dollars, more than contracted, and its report also named former governor Charles Sirleaf. Crane denied wrongdoing and kickbacks and said it had not been charged. This is an allegation and no court has found it proven.
n:Goznak: Goznak is the Russian state printer, based in Moscow. It printed Libyan dinars for the eastern central bank in Benghazi and Bayda, which is not internationally recognized. Russian customs data cited by Reuters showed 4.5 billion dinars shipped between February and June 2019. On 1 November 2019 Malta seized two containers of the notes, citing United Nations resolutions that recognize only the government in Tripoli.
n:Giesecke+Devrient: Giesecke+Devrient is a banknote printer based in Munich, Germany, tied to 15 central banks. The Central Bank of Kenya disclosed a five-year deal with the firm worth 14.2 billion shillings, or 109,422,740 US dollars, reported on 21 August 2024. The Deutsche Bundesbank's banknote tender for 2012 gave it 526 million 10-euro notes. Asked how it picked the printer for the Central Bank of Armenia's third banknote series, the bank's representative said Giesecke+Devrient 'won as a result of a comprehensive evaluation of all offers'. Single notes or note families are recorded for Eswatini (20 lilangeni), Tajikistan (a commemorative 100 somoni note put into circulation on 30 October 2025), Malawi (2,000 kwacha), Mongolia (5,000 togrog), the Bahamas (1 dollar, introduced on 3 February 2025), Suriname (500 dollars), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (100 and 200 franc notes carrying the firm's Munich imprint), Oman (a commemorative 1 rial polymer note introduced on 11 January 2026), Eritrea (the current nakfa series) Azerbaijan (the renewed 50 manat note) and Georgia (the 200 lari note, which the National Bank of Georgia said in 2007 was produced at the firm; the record covers that denomination only). In Myanmar the customer was the state-owned Security Print Works rather than the central bank: the firm supplied raw materials, supplies and system components for printing kyat banknotes, and said in a release issued in 2021 that it had suspended all deliveries after the military crackdown.
n:Nigeria Security Printing and Minting: The Nigeria Security Printing and Minting Company (NSPMC) is a printing firm in Nigeria, shown on the map at the country rather than at its office. It printed the redesigned 2022 naira notes for the Central Bank of Nigeria. The anti-corruption agency EFCC verified payments from the central bank to the company as part of its four-count prosecution of former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele, who is charged with unlawfully printing new notes. These are charges, not a conviction.

Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:FVCbank (FVCBankcorp, Inc.): FVCbank (FVCBankcorp, Inc.), based in Fairfax, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $3,586,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Beacon Financial Corp. (bank subsidiar: Beacon Financial Corp. (bank subsidiary) is in the United States, and its bank subsidiary owns shares in the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States. It holds $57,407,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Citizens & Northern Bank (Citizens & N: Citizens & Northern Bank (Citizens & Northern Corp.), based in Wellsboro, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $7,637,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:The Park National Bank (Park National: The Park National Bank (Park National Corp.), based in Newark, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $14,653,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Southern Bank (Southern Missouri Banco: Southern Bank (Southern Missouri Bancorp, Inc.), based in Poplar Bluff, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $9,139,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (as of 30 June 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Landmark National Bank (Landmark Banco: Landmark National Bank (Landmark Bancorp, Inc.), based in Manhattan, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $3,000,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Plumas Bank (Plumas Bancorp): Plumas Bank (Plumas Bancorp), based in Quincy, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $3,565,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco (as of 31 December 2025). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:National Printing Bureau: The National Printing Bureau is an incorporated administrative agency in Japan that makes the country's banknotes. The Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, says on its page (undated) that Japanese banknotes are manufactured by the Bureau and that the Bank receives them from it.
n:Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Pri: Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited is a banknote printing company in India. It says the Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank, set it up as a wholly owned subsidiary on 3 February 1995 to add to banknote production. It runs presses at Mysore and Salboni, and it prints banknotes for the Reserve Bank.
n:Pakistan Security Printing Corporation: Pakistan Security Printing Corporation is a state printing works in Pakistan that prints banknotes for the State Bank of Pakistan, the country's central bank. On 5 July 2017 the State Bank said it had acquired the corporation's banknote and prize bond printing functions from the Federal Government.
n:China Banknote Printing and Minting Co: China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation is a state printing works in China. Bloomberg Línea reported on 21 November 2024 that the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (known as the BCRA) had ordered 230 million notes from it. Crane Currency and others were accredited only to bid on a further tender, so they are not counted as printers for the bank.
Joh. Enschedé Banknotes B.V. is a banknote printing firm in Haarlem, Netherlands. It prints banknotes for Deutsche Bundesbank, the central bank of Germany. The Bundesbank's banknote tender for 2012 awarded it 752 million €50 notes (Deutsche Bundesbank, 29.07.2011).
n:Bundesdruckerei GmbH: Bundesdruckerei GmbH is a printing company based in Berlin, Germany. Deutsche Bundesbank, Germany's central bank, awarded it 298 million 100-euro notes and 50 million 200-euro notes in its banknote tender for 2012, which concluded on 29 July 2011.
n:Banque de France printing works, Chama: The Banque de France printing works at Chamalières, France, belongs to the Bank of France, the country's central bank, and prints its banknotes. According to the bank's page (undated), it prints more than 2.5 billion notes a year, in euros and in the currencies of some 20 countries.
n:EuropaFi: EuropaFi is a subsidiary of the Banque de France, based in France. It makes the banknote paper for the Bank of France (undated page), which prints the notes at its own works.
n:Banknote Printing Plant, Central Bank: The Banknote Printing Plant in Türkiye operates under the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, the country's central bank. According to the bank's page (undated), Turkish banknotes are printed there.
n:Orell Füssli: Orell Füssli is a banknote printer based in Zürich, Switzerland, tied to four central banks. At home it prints the Swiss franc: the Swiss National Bank states that Orell Füssli Security Printing Ltd prints the ninth series of Swiss franc banknotes, and Swissinfo reported on 17 April 2019 that the firm has a contract with the bank to produce counterfeit-proof notes. LexLatin reported on 27 March 2024 that it was partially awarded a tender to print and supply banknotes for Nicaragua. El Observador reports, quoting the Central Bank of Costa Rica's Treasury director, that it prints the 1,000 and 10,000 colon polymer notes, while Oberthur Fiduciaire printed the 2,000, 5,000 and 20,000; that article spells the name "Orell Fuslli". Wikipedia's article on the Israeli new shekel names the firm as a printer of those notes, which is a weaker source than the others here.
n:Canadian Bank Note Company, Limited: Canadian Bank Note Company, Limited is a printing company in Ottawa, Canada. The Bank of Canada, the country's central bank, named it among the printers of its polymer (plastic) banknote series in a 2011 backgrounder. Notes in that series began circulating in 2011.
BA International Inc. is a printing company in Ottawa, Canada. The Bank of Canada, the country's central bank, named it among the printers of its polymer (plastic) banknote series in a 2011 backgrounder. Notes in that series began circulating in 2011.
n:Casa da Moeda: Casa da Moeda is Brazil's state mint. It signed a contract with the Central Bank of Brazil on 13 April 2017 to print 980 million banknotes, worth R$ 279.14 million (Brazilian reais). Tribuna do Paraná reported that the bank hired it at a price up to 41% higher than the one charged by Sweden.
n:Comptroller and Auditor General: The Comptroller and Auditor General, an auditor in Ireland, audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Ireland (2025), according to the bank's Annual Report 2025 and Annual Performance Statement 2025-2026. Grant Thornton also audits the bank's accounts.
Ernst & Young Audit, s.r.o. is an audit firm in Prague, Czechia. It audits the accounts of the Czech National Bank (2025), according to the independent auditor's report in the bank's Annual Report 2025.
n:KPMG Auditores Consultores Limitada: KPMG Auditores Consultores Limitada is an audit firm in Santiago, Chile. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Chile (2025), according to the independent auditors' report in the bank's 2025 financial statements.
n:KPMG Audyt Spółka z ograniczoną odpowi: KPMG Audyt Spółka z ograniczoną odpowiedzialnością sp.k. is an auditing firm in Warsaw, Poland. An auditor checks an organisation's accounts and reports on them. It audited the accounts of the National Bank of Poland, the country's central bank, for 2025.
n:B1 - Audit LLC (OOO «Б1 - Аудит»): B1 - Audit LLC is an audit firm in Russia. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Russia (2025), according to the Bank of Russia Annual Report 2025 (National Financial Council decisions).
n:Accounts Chamber of the Russian Federa: The Accounts Chamber of the Russian Federation is a state audit body in Russia. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Russia (2025), according to the bank's Annual Report 2025.
n:National Audit Office (audit authority: The National Audit Office is the audit authority under the State Council, China's government. Article 40 of the law on the People's Bank of China, China's central bank (2003 amendment), provides that the Office audits the bank's accounts.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers (on behalf of t: PricewaterhouseCoopers is an accounting firm with an office in Wellington, New Zealand. It audited the accounts of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, the country's central bank, for 2022/23, acting on behalf of the Auditor-General. The bank's 2023 annual report records this.
n:Kost Forer Gabbay & Kasierer (Ernst &: Kost Forer Gabbay & Kasierer (Ernst & Young Israel) is an audit firm in Tel Aviv, Israel. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Israel (2019), according to the bank's Auditors' report 2019.
n:KPMG Professional Services: KPMG Professional Services is an audit firm in Nigeria. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Nigeria (2024). The source is The Sun (Nigeria), whose May 2025 article is headed 'CBN records N38.8bn profit in 2024'.
n:Baker Tilly GmbH & Co. KG Wirtschaftsp: Baker Tilly GmbH & Co. KG Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft is an auditing firm in Munich, Germany. On 2 June 2025 the European Central Bank recommended it as auditor of the accounts of Deutsche Bundesbank, Germany's central bank, for financial year 2027. A Council of the EU document records the recommendation.
n:Auditor General del Banco de la Repúbl: The Auditor General is an office inside the Bank of the Republic, Colombia's central bank, that audits the bank's accounts. Its report on the year ended 31 December 2024 is dated 27 January 2025.
n:SizweNtsalubaGobodo Grant Thornton Inc: SizweNtsalubaGobodo Grant Thornton Inc. is an auditing firm in South Africa. It audited the accounts of the South African Reserve Bank, the country's central bank, for the year ended 31 March 2023. Its independent auditors' report is dated 12 June 2023.
n:Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan (BPK), Republ: Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan (BPK) is Indonesia's state audit body. It audits the accounts of Bank Indonesia, the country's central bank. Kontan reported on 25 June 2025 that Bank Indonesia again received an unqualified opinion (a clean audit result) from the BPK for 2024.
n:French Treasury: The French Treasury is a government body based in Paris, France. It is tied to 15 central banks, and ten of them are: the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) as it operates in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo, and the Bank of Central African States (BEAC) in Cameroon and the Central African Republic. In each case the tie is a guarantee. France backs the currency the bank issues under a cooperation agreement. The West African CFA franc is fixed at 1 euro for 655.957 CFA francs, and France promises unconditional and unlimited convertibility, meaning it advances money to the central bank if its foreign exchange reserves run out. The Central African CFA franc has the same rate. The euro replaced the French franc as its anchor on 1 January 1999 with no change in the rate, and France commits euro funds if the region cannot pay for imports in foreign currency. These are cooperation arrangements, and the text reports no wrongdoing.
n:Government of Portugal: The Government of Portugal is based in Lisbon, Portugal. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Cape Verde. Portugal guarantees the currency that bank issues, the Cabo Verde escudo, under a cooperation agreement on exchange rates. The agreement, called the Acordo de Cooperação Cambial, was signed on 13 March 1998. The rate was set at 0.55 Cape Verde escudos per Portuguese escudo, and it became 110.265 Cape Verde escudos per euro. This is a currency arrangement between the two countries, and no wrongdoing is reported.
n:Argentine judiciary: The Argentine judiciary, the country's court system, features in a dispute over who controls the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic. In a page dated 30 January 2010, Argentina's central bank chief Martin Perez Redrado resigned amid a dispute with President Cristina Kirchner. An Argentine court had determined that Kirchner needed the approval of the full Congress to use the bank's reserves, and the reserves stayed frozen while lawmakers were expected to take the matter up in March.
n:Bank of Ceylon: Bank of Ceylon is a bank based in Colombo, Sri Lanka. An Anti-Corruption Commission report made public in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority, the Maldives' central bank, negligent over the embezzlement of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. Its Financial Intelligence Unit, the office that examines suspicious money, was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque from that company to a firm called SOF, did not investigate it properly, and never looked at SOF's large transactions through Bank of Maldives and Bank of Ceylon.
n:CLICO: CLICO is an insurer based in Port of Spain, Trinidad & Tobago. At the Commission of Enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union, Queen's Counsel Peter Carter put it to former Central Bank governor Ewart Williams on 6 December 2012 that if the bank had intervened in 2006, over 10 billion Trinidad and Tobago dollars would not have been at risk. Williams said the bank saw warning signs at CLICO in 2006 but held off to avoid a run, and intervened in 2009. That was cross-examination, not a commission finding, so it is unproven.
n:Commission of Inquiry into the financi: This was a Gambian public inquiry, based in Banjul, into the finances of former president Yahya Jammeh, and it examined the Central Bank of The Gambia. The government's White Paper accepted its finding that between September 2015 and January 2017 General Sulayman Badjie, purportedly acting for Jammeh, instructed the Governor or his deputies to withdraw US dollars, and that the Governor handed cash to soldiers. The Commission held Badjie accountable for illegal withdrawals of 15,785,601 US dollars, 300,000 euros and 9,606,000 dalasis, and the government ordered the money recovered by forfeiting and selling his properties. It also records 28.5 million US dollars illegally granted in the bank's 3M Account in 2000 and 2001.
n:Direccion de Persecucion de la Corrupc: This is the Dominican Republic's office for prosecuting corruption in public administration, based in Santo Domingo. It took former central bank governor Jose Lois Malkun, former deputy governor Felix Calvo, former administrative director Cesar Apolinar Veloz and former legal counsel Manuel Rubio Cristoforis to court on charges including breach of trust and criminal association, over the disappearance of 18 promissory notes worth 10,663 million Dominican pesos said to have been handed fraudulently to former banker Manuel Arturo Pellerano. The charges are unproven. The central bank did not complain or join as a civil party; a Junta Monetaria resolution said its authorities were negotiating the notes' return.
n:Farmers Bank: Farmers Bank is a bank in Eswatini. In 2017 an evaluations team at the Central Bank of Eswatini recommended refusing it a commercial banking licence, and the application was turned down late that year. In May 2018 finance minister Martin Dlamini told the central bank the king had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it, and a conditional licence followed in September 2018 after a royal command from King Mswati III. The central bank revoked it on 5 October 2020 because the source of the seed capital was unexplained; commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled that December that the bank should keep it, and the central bank reinstated it in January 2021. A 2022 Kroll report said outside parties had likely instructed the central bank to proceed, and that 89 million rand of seed capital went into silver bullion the central bank could not verify existed.
n:Hindu Credit Union: The Hindu Credit Union was a lender in Trinidad & Tobago whose collapse, with that of CL Financial, was examined by a commission of enquiry commissioned in November 2010 under sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman. It found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers to regulate insurers 'fundamentally deficient', because of the narrow scope of the Insurance Act, and said the Inspector of financial institutions used the limited tools available but that Clico and CL Financial management largely ignored them. It blamed no named Central Bank official, and sat from March 2011 to May 2013.
n:Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court: The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court sits in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. It sentenced businessmen Farijala Hussein and Rajabu Maranda to five years in prison, finding them guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. A report published on 27 May 2011 describes these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 Bank of Tanzania corruption scandal.
n:Manuel Arturo Pellerano: Manuel Arturo Pellerano is a former banker in the Dominican Republic. The country's office for prosecuting corruption in public administration took former central bank governor Jose Lois Malkun, former deputy governor Felix Calvo, former administrative director Cesar Apolinar Veloz and former legal counsel Manuel Rubio Cristoforis to court on charges including breach of trust and criminal association, over the disappearance of 18 promissory notes worth 10,663 million Dominican pesos said to have been handed fraudulently to Pellerano. The charges are unproven. The central bank did not complain or join as a civil party; a Junta Monetaria resolution said its authorities were negotiating the notes' return with him.
n:Ministerio Publico de Chile: The Ministerio Publico is Chile's public prosecution service, based in Santiago. In March 2022 someone posing as the chief financial officer of the US firm RVK emailed the Central Bank of Chile a false invoice for 205,000 US dollars from an address one letter different from the real one, and the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors on 20 May 2022 and opened an internal investigation, saying there was no indication any official took part deliberately. It dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022; he sued in December, calling the dismissal abusive and seeking 267 million pesos.
n:Nicolae Timofti: Nicolae Timofti was president of Moldova, based in Chisinau. Dorin Dragutanu resigned as governor of the National Bank of Moldova after criticism for failing to prevent about 1 billion US dollars disappearing from three Moldovan banks in 2014. He said he was resigning because of pressure from some politicians, and denied responsibility, saying he had repeatedly warned the authorities. Timofti and Prime Minister Valeriu Strelet had both said he should be removed.
n:Paetongtarn Shinawatra: Paetongtarn Shinawatra leads the Pheu Thai Party in Bangkok. She criticised the Bank of Thailand's independence, saying the law that keeps the bank separate from the government obstructs solving economic problems. The remarks drew a backlash, and Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin said he had no plans to remove Governor Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput or to amend the Bank of Thailand Act. A 2008 amendment to that Act makes removing the governor over policy disagreements very difficult.
n:RVK: RVK is a firm based in the United States. In March 2022 someone posing as its chief financial officer emailed the Central Bank of Chile a false invoice for 205,000 US dollars, from an address differing from the real one by a single letter, and asked for payment to a new account at another bank; the bank paid. The bank complained to the public prosecution service in May 2022 and dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022; he sued in December, calling the dismissal abusive and unfair and seeking 267 million pesos.
n:Seoul Central District Court: The Seoul Central District Court sits in Seoul, South Korea. A former Bank of Korea employee, moved in 2013 to the museum operations team and responsible for paying in the proceeds of the bank's publication sales, diverted about 56 million won in 14 transfers to a personal account and used a corporate card to buy about 12 million won of commemorative uncut banknote sheets. Judge Lee Heung-kwon convicted the employee of occupational breach of trust and embezzlement and imposed eight months in prison suspended for two years, noting the full amount had been repaid.
n:Supreme Court of Appeal of Bahrain: The Supreme Court of Appeal of Bahrain sits in Manama. It upheld a Court of First Instance ruling convicting the Central Bank of Iran, together with a number of Iranian banks, Future Bank and six Future Bank officials, as announced by attorney general Wael Bualai. Each convicted party, including the Central Bank of Iran, was fined one million Bahraini dinars; five Future Bank officials received ten-year prison sentences and the sixth five years. The court upheld confiscation of remittances put at 184 million US dollars, 967 million euros, 53 million dirhams and 235 billion Iranian rials.
n:Transitional government of Madagascar: Madagascar's transitional government, based in Antananarivo, dismissed central bank governor Frederic Rasamoely in February 2012. Bank employees staged a sit-in, saying the removal went against the bank's independence, and said the strike would continue while they challenged the new governor's appointment.
n:Wlodzimierz Czarzasty: Wlodzimierz Czarzasty is Marshal of the Sejm, Poland's lower house of parliament. In October 2026 the Sejm's Committee on Constitutional Responsibility adopted a report supporting the referral of National Bank of Poland president Adam Glapinski to the State Tribunal, and Czarzasty said the full chamber would vote in the second half of November 2026. The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses Glapinski of indirectly financing the budget deficit through asset purchases in 2020 and 2021 and of acting without proper authorisation from the Monetary Policy Council. Glapinski and the bank called the allegations baseless, and no vote had been held.
n:AKO Foundation: The AKO Foundation is a charity in the United Kingdom. In August 2020, after the Storting's finance committee raised conflict-of-interest concerns, Norges Bank's Executive Board rewrote the terms of its incoming investment chief, Nicolai Tangen: he would sell his holding in AKO Capital, transfer that holding and its dividend rights to the AKO Foundation with no ownership interest in AKO Capital in perpetuity, and hold his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said his appointment had breached guidelines, regulations and laws. Tangen took office on 1 September.
n:Art-B: Art-B was a Polish company at the centre of a cheque-float scheme, in which money is drawn against cheques that have not yet cleared. Its owners fled in the summer of 1991, and arrests followed. Among those arrested was Grzegorz Wojtowicz, president of Narodowy Bank Polski, the country's central bank. He was charged with unintentionally causing bank losses of about 72 billion old zloty, and the court acquitted him. Prison sentences went to several employees of state banks.
n:Bank of Georgia: Bank of Georgia is a commercial bank in Tbilisi. At a briefing on 20 September 2023 the acting president of the National Bank of Georgia, Natia Turnava, confirmed she had single-handedly changed the procedure for carrying out sanctions regimes, adopting it on 19 September and making it effective the next day, and said she had told National Bank Council members in advance. Bank of Georgia and TBC Bank had frozen the accounts of Otar Partskhaladze; Turnava said they broke no law, because the amendment took effect the day she spoke. Vice-president Papuna Lezhava resigned.
n:Caixa Geral de Depositos: Caixa Geral de Depositos is a bank in Lisbon. In April 2019, after an EY audit of CGD's management, the Bank of Portugal's ethics committee examined a request by governor Carlos Costa to be excused from matters concerning CGD. Costa had sat on CGD's board from 2004 to 2006 and may have taken part in extended credit council meetings that approved operations which caused losses, while now heading the supervisor assessing former CGD directors. Vice-governor Elisa Ferreira did not recuse herself but reported a possible conflict over her husband's past role at La Seda. The committee's conclusions were not made public.
n:Constitutional Tribunal of Poland: The Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw decides whether Polish laws fit the constitution. The ruling coalition accused National Bank of Poland governor Adam Glapinski of breaking several laws and of failing to uphold the bank's political independence under the former Law and Justice government, and in March 2024 it asked the Sejm to bring him before the State Tribunal, which tries holders of high office. A ruling of 12 January 2024 had set the bar at a three-fifths majority, and the coalition held 241 of 460 seats against a threshold of 276. On 20 August 2024 a five-judge panel including chief justice Julia Przylebska ruled the legislation allowing him to be brought before the constitutional accountability committee unconstitutional.
n:District Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw: The District Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw is the state prosecution service for the Polish capital. It is investigating how information classified as secret got out of the closed part of the National Bank of Poland's Monetary Policy Council meeting of 8 September 2023, after a complaint by one of the Council's members. A court had earlier overturned a decision refusing to open the investigation. On 12 June 2025 prosecutors secured documents at the bank's head office, after the bank had twice refused to hand them over.
n:Financial Action Task Force: The Financial Action Task Force, based in Paris, sets the international standards countries are judged against on money laundering, and keeps a grey list of those whose enforcement it finds wanting. It added Mongolia to that list over money-laundering enforcement, and Mongolian lawmakers accepted the resignation of central bank governor Nadmid Bayartsaikhan on 21 November 2019, after he resigned over the listing. Parliament appointed Byadran Lkhagvasuren the next day.
n:Inter-American Development Bank: The Inter-American Development Bank, based in Washington, D.C., lends for development in Latin America and the Caribbean. Karnit Flug, who later ran Israel's central bank, worked there as a senior research economist from 1994 to 1996. She had joined the International Monetary Fund as an economist in 1984 and the Bank of Israel's Research Department in 1988. She became Deputy Governor of the Bank of Israel in July 2011 and was appointed Governor on 13 November 2013.
n:Kroll: Kroll is a corporate investigations firm in the United States, commissioned by the Central Bank of Eswatini. In 2017 the bank's evaluations team recommended refusing Farmers Bank a commercial banking licence, warning it would tarnish the integrity of the bank's licensing policy, and the application was rejected; a conditional licence followed in September 2018 after a royal command from King Mswati III. Governor Majozi Sithole said he was given a royal command to attend a meeting about the bank on 14 July 2017, and in May 2018 finance minister Martin Dlamini said the king had ordered an investigation into the bank's reluctance to license it. The central bank revoked the licence on 5 October 2020 over the unexplained source of the seed capital; commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled in December 2020 that it should be kept, and the bank reinstated it in January 2021 while objecting to procedural improprieties. Kroll's 2022 report said third parties outside the bank had likely intervened and instructed it to proceed, and that 89 million rand of seed capital had gone from 2019 into silver bullion the bank could not verify existed.
n:Manuel Chang: Manuel Chang, of Mozambique, is named in the hidden debts case, over more than two billion US dollars of loans from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia to the companies Proindicus, Ematum and MAM. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, the 49th day of a trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove testified as a witness that he signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed personally to senior bank officials by Eugenio Matlaba and Antonio Carlos do Rosario rather than submitted at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. The Foreign Exchange Law regulations bar the bank from authorising foreign loans to private companies whose repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove said the bar applied only to guarantees obtained after loans were agreed, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected that reading. Bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified the same day that the loans should not have been authorised, and that Gove told her to work only with the management group and leave technical staff out.
n:Ministry of Finance of Chile: The Ministry of Finance of Chile, in Santiago, is named alongside a fraud at the Banco Central de Chile. On 11 May 2022 a consultant under contract to the central bank told it that it had not been paid for services provided in 2021. The bank had paid 205,000 US dollars, about 170 million pesos, into the account of someone posing as an international consulting services provider. It complained to prosecutors on 20 May 2022 and investigated possible administrative responsibilities internally, saying nothing indicated any official took part deliberately.
n:Nina Angelovska: Nina Angelovska was finance minister of North Macedonia. An association of Eurostandard Bank depositors said in a press release that the central bank governor had tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was put under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so the bank could keep operating. It said Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted. No charges have been brought and no official finding made, so none of this is proven.
n:Peter Carter: Peter Carter is a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister, who appeared at the Commission of Enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union in Trinidad and Tobago. On 6 December 2012 he put it to former Central Bank governor Ewart Williams that had the Central Bank intervened in 2006, more than 10 billion Trinidad and Tobago dollars would not have been at risk. Williams had said the bank saw early warning signs at the insurer CLICO in 2006 but held off to avoid a run on it, and intervened in 2009. This was cross-examination, not a finding by the commission.
n:Rajabu Maranda: Rajabu Maranda is a businessman in Tanzania. The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court in Dar es Salaam found him and fellow businessman Farijala Hussein guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, sentenced each to five years in prison, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. A report published on 27 May 2011 describes these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 corruption scandal at the Bank of Tanzania.
n:Srettha Thavisin: Srettha Thavisin was prime minister of Thailand, in Bangkok. Pheu Thai Party leader Paetongtarn Shinawatra criticised the Bank of Thailand's independence, saying the law that keeps the bank separate from the government obstructs solving economic problems. The remarks drew a backlash, and Srettha said he had no plans to remove Governor Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput or to amend the Bank of Thailand Act. A 2008 amendment to that Act makes removing the governor over policy disagreements very difficult.
n:Tribunal de Sentencia de Asuncion: The Tribunal de Sentencia de Asuncion is a sentencing court in Paraguay's capital. On 6 June 2006, presided over by Sandra Farias with Gustavo Amarilla and Miguel Said, it sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as the alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Banco Central had intervened in and declared bankrupt. Jose Pecci, the bank's former superintendent, got eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor had sought ten years.
n:Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi: Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi was Yemen's president, based in Aden. He dismissed the governor of the Central Bank of Yemen and his deputy, according to the state news agency Saba, and Ahmed bin Ahmed Ghaleb Al-Maabq was named governor with Muhammad Omar Banaja as deputy. No reason was given for the removals, which were the fourth such sacking since the country's civil war began.
n:Assembleia da República committee of i: This was a committee of inquiry set up by Portugal's parliament, the Assembleia da República in Lisbon, to examine losses at the bank Novo Banco. On 20 July 2021 its rapporteur, Fernando Anastácio, presented a proposed final report saying supervision had failed across the board and that there was a permanent and systematic failure; that was a draft, and the PSD said its deputies would vote against it and propose amendments. On Tuesday 27 July 2021 the committee approved its final report, with the PS voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concludes that the winding up of Banco Espírito Santo and the initial capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, and it leaves criticism of the Bank of Portugal and the European Commission; the criticisms are not set out and no Bank of Portugal officials are named.
n:Bank of Maldives: The Bank of Maldives is a bank in Malé. It is named in the case of money embezzled from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. An Anti-Corruption Commission report made public in February 2019 found the country's central bank, the Maldives Monetary Authority, negligent over the theft of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from that company: its Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque to a firm called SOF, and did not examine SOF's large transactions passing through the Bank of Maldives and the Bank of Ceylon.
n:Cambio Nelson: Cambio Nelson is a company in Uruguay. Investigating fraud at the firm, prosecutor Rodrigo Morosoli asked for the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, for joint responsibility in a continued crime of misappropriation. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and the prosecutor appealed in April 2017.
n:Cour des comptes (DRC): The Cour des comptes is a state audit court in Kinshasa, DR Congo, and it has been examining Deogratias Mutombo, a former governor of the Central Bank of the Congo. On 25 October 2023 it was reported that his accounts, and those of Albert Yuma, former board chairman of the mining company Gecamines, had been frozen, and that both men must stay available to the court. The sum at issue is an alleged embezzlement of 25.521 million US dollars, which is unproven.
n:Ematum: Ematum was a Mozambican company whose foreign borrowing, with that of Proindicus and MAM, made up the country's hidden debts: more than two billion US dollars from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he had signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities in how the central bank granted them. Bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified the same day that it should not have approved the loans, which included 850 million dollars for Ematum in August 2013.
n:First Labour Court of Santiago: The First Labour Court of Santiago in Chile hears employment disputes. In March 2022 someone posing as the chief financial officer of the US firm RVK emailed the Central Bank of Chile a false invoice for 205,000 US dollars, from an address one letter different from the real one, and asked for payment to a new account; the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors in May 2022 and dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022 over the payment. In December he sued in this court, calling the dismissal abusive and seeking 267 million Chilean pesos.
n:Jaan Naaber: Jaan Naaber was a prosecutor in Estonia. A Tallinn court had acquitted Siim Kallas, a former president of the Bank of Estonia, of charges tied to a failed investment deal made during his time at the central bank. On 15 March 1999 Naaber appealed against that acquittal, asking a district court to convict Kallas and an unnamed co-defendant over their role in the deal.
n:Luis Gonzalez Macchi: Luis Gonzalez Macchi was a president of Paraguay. On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion presided over by Sandra Farias gave him six years in prison for breach of trust as the alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Central Bank of Paraguay had taken over and declared bankrupt. Jose Pecci, a former superintendent at the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor, Victoria Acuna, had asked for ten years.
n:Maputo City Court: The Maputo City Court in Mozambique heard the hidden debts trial of 19 people, over loans of more than two billion US dollars from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM. Giving evidence on 23 November 2021, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he had signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed to senior bank officials in person rather than filed at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. Judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his reading of the rule barring such loans.
n:Mswati III: Mswati III is the king of Eswatini. In 2017 an evaluations team at the Central Bank of Eswatini recommended refusing a commercial banking licence to Farmers Bank. A conditional licence was issued in September 2018 after a royal command from the king. It was revoked in October 2020 because Farmers Bank could not prove where its seed capital came from, and an appeal chaired by commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo reinstated it in January 2021. A 2022 report by Kroll said outside parties had probably told the bank to proceed, and that 89 million rand of the seed capital had gone from 2019 into silver bullion the bank could not verify existed.
n:Note Printing Works, Bank of Thailand: The Note Printing Works at Nakhon Pathom is the Bank of Thailand's own banknote plant. The bank's history of the works records that the Cabinet authorised the bank to establish it in 1961, and describes the new works as built for the production of Thai banknotes.
n:Petro Poroshenko: Petro Poroshenko was president of Ukraine, in Kyiv. Valeria Gontareva stepped down as governor of the National Bank of Ukraine on 10 May 2017, but by January 2018 parliament had still not voted on her resignation or on a replacement. She had been on unpaid leave since 26 September, saying she would stay away until parliament acted. On 18 January 2018 Poroshenko nominated the acting head, Yakiv Smolii, for the post.
n:RenaissanceRe Holdings: RenaissanceRe Holdings is a reinsurance company based in Pembroke, Bermuda. In November 2024 Loretta Mester joined its board of directors. She had been president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland from 2014 until she retired in 2024, and over those same years sat on the Federal Open Market Committee, the group that sets interest rates in the United States.
n:State Great Khural of Mongolia: The State Great Khural is Mongolia's parliament, in Ulaanbaatar. On 21 November 2019 lawmakers accepted the resignation of the governor of the Bank of Mongolia, Nadmid Bayartsaikhan. He stepped down after the Financial Action Task Force, the international body that sets standards against money laundering, added Mongolia to its grey list over its enforcement. The next day parliament appointed Byadran Lkhagvasuren in his place.
n:Surapong Suebwonglee: Surapong Suebwonglee was Thailand's finance minister. In 2008 he appointed Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi to the committee that selects members of the Bank of Thailand's board; all three were representatives of financial institutions that the Bank of Thailand supervises. The National Anti-Corruption Commission filed the case on 27 May 2015, and the Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted him of malfeasance in office. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and fined 20,000 baht.
n:Trifun Kostovski: Trifun Kostovski is named in North Macedonia in connection with the failure of Eurostandard Bank. An association of the bank's depositors said the governor of the central bank tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was placed under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so it could keep operating. The association said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted, and that over 60 million euros were lost. No charges and no official finding are recorded.
n:Zephyr Management LP: Zephyr Management LP is a private equity firm in New York. Dennis P. Lockhart worked there from 2001 to 2003, after Citibank from 1971 to 1988 and Heller Financial from 1988 to 2001, and then served as president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta from 1 March 2007 to 28 February 2017.
n:Anthony Akoto Osei: Anthony Akoto Osei is a politician in Accra and a figure in Ghana's New Patriotic Party. After the party won the 2016 election, the position of Bank of Ghana governor Abdul Nashiru Issahaku came under scrutiny, and Osei held that he should voluntarily step down. Issahaku resigned with effect after 1 April 2017, telling Joy Business he was leaving for personal reasons, following an agreement reached with the government earlier that month. A governor's four-year term is protected by Article 183(4)(d) of Ghana's 1992 constitution.
n:BSP Security Plant Complex: The BSP Security Plant Complex is a plant in Quezon City run by Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines. It is where the country's banknotes are made: a speech by the bank's governor, Benjamin Diokno, published by the Bank for International Settlements, describes the complex as the facility that has housed the Bangko Sentral's currency production since 1978.
n:Belarusian Interbank Settlement Center: The Belarusian Interbank Settlement Center is a company in Minsk, named in a bribery case around the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus. At a trial reported in March 2020, prosecutors charged Feliks Kasperovich, with Andrei Podgorny of the National Bank's information technology directorate, with taking bribes of at least 868,750 US dollars from 2007 onwards. Igor Kudasov, head of the bank's payment systems directorate, was charged over a 30,000 dollar bribe and had been held since 29 December 2018. Kasperovich admitted the charges; the rest are unproven.
n:Cayman Islands Football Association: The Cayman Islands Football Association is the islands' football body. In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, which acts as the central bank there, said it would review the involvement of local people and financial institutions in the FIFA corruption case, after Caymanian businessman Jeffrey Webb was arrested in Switzerland on 27 May. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the association under Webb and was with him at the arrest. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would remain and that no Cayman bank was shown to have done wrong.
n:Criminal Court of the Maldives: The Criminal Court of the Maldives sits in Male. In February 2020 prosecutors charged Ibrahim Athif Shakoor, former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit at the Maldives Monetary Authority, with negligence over the MMPRC case, in which state funds were moved to private accounts. He denied the allegations, saying he had told the then governor, Azeema Adam, about the illegal transactions. At a hearing in September 2020 he sought a deal waiving prison in exchange for admitting a breach of the money laundering law. The charges were later withdrawn.
n:Ernst & Young Audit Services LLC: Ernst & Young Audit Services LLC is an audit firm based in Kyiv. An audit is an outside check of whether an organisation's accounts are accurate. This firm does that work for the National Bank of Ukraine, the country's central bank, and signed the bank's consolidated financial statements for the financial year ending 31 December 2024.
n:Gecamines: Gecamines is a company in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It appears in a case around the Central Bank of the Congo, the country's central bank. On 25 October 2023 Financial Afrik reported that the accounts of former central bank governor Deogratias Mutombo, and those of former Gecamines board chairman Albert Yuma, had been frozen, and that both men must remain available to the Cour des comptes, the state audit court. The sum at issue is alleged embezzlement of 25.521 million US dollars. It is not proven.
n:Jeffrey Webb: Jeffrey Webb is a Caymanian businessman, arrested in Switzerland on 27 May 2015 in the FIFA corruption case. In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, which acts as the central bank there, said it would review the involvement of local people and financial institutions in that case. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the Cayman Islands Football Association under Webb and was with him at the arrest. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would stay as managing director and that no Cayman bank was shown to have done wrong.
n:MAM: MAM is a Mozambican company, one of three state-linked borrowers in the hidden debts case, with Proindicus and Ematum; their loans from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia came to more than two billion US dollars. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove testified that he signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security. Rules bar the bank from authorising such loans when repayment depends on a state guarantee, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected Gove's argument to the contrary. The bank's own administrator told the court it should not have authorised them.
n:Martin Dlamini: Martin Dlamini was finance minister of Eswatini. The Central Bank of Eswatini rejected Farmers Bank's application for a commercial banking licence in late 2017, and in May 2018 Dlamini told the bank that the king had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it. The licence was granted after a royal command in September 2018. The central bank revoked it on 5 October 2020 over the unexplained source of the seed capital, then reinstated it in January 2021, objecting to procedural improprieties, after commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled that Farmers Bank should keep it.
n:National Anti-Corruption Commission (T: The National Anti-Corruption Commission is a state agency in Bangkok that investigates officials. On 27 May 2015 it filed the case in which the Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance. In 2008 he had appointed Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi to the committee that selects Bank of Thailand board members, and all three represented financial institutions the bank supervises. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a 20,000 baht fine.
n:Novo Banco: Novo Banco is a bank in Lisbon, created out of the collapsed Banco Espirito Santo. On Tuesday 27 July 2021 a Portuguese parliamentary committee of inquiry approved its final report on it, with the Socialist Party voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concludes that the resolution of Banco Espirito Santo and the initial capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, and it criticises the Bank of Portugal, the country's central bank, and the European Commission.
n:Polska Wytwórnia Papierów Wartościowyc: Polska Wytwornia Papierow Wartosciowych S.A. is a security printing firm in Warsaw. It makes Poland's banknotes: the National Bank of Poland, Narodowy Bank Polski, states in its own publication on banknote security features that Polish notes are produced by this firm, which the bank commissions to do the work.
n:Rodrigo Morosoli: Rodrigo Morosoli is a prosecutor in Uruguay. Investigating the Cambio Nelson fraud, he sought the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, for co-authorship of a continued crime of misappropriation, which means taking money held in trust. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and Morosoli appealed that decision in April 2017. Nothing against Capote was established.
n:State Prosecutor General of the Republ: The State Prosecutor General of the Republic of Slovenia heads the country's prosecution service in Ljubljana, and the post was then held by Mr Fiser. Slovenian authorities searched the premises of Banka Slovenije, the central bank, on 6 July 2016 in a pre-criminal investigation procedure, a step in the long-running inquiry into Slovenia's 2013 bank bailout. The central bank then published letters from the President of the European Central Bank to Fiser, and to European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker, about European Central Bank information seized during the search.
n:Szymon Holownia: Szymon Holownia is a politician in Poland. The ruling coalition accused National Bank of Poland governor Adam Glapinski of breaking several laws and of failing to keep the bank politically independent under the former Law and Justice government, and in March 2024 it moved in the Sejm, the lower house, to bring him before the State Tribunal. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal ruled that legislation unconstitutional; in January 2024 it had also required a three-fifths majority, and the coalition held 241 of 460 seats against a threshold of 276.
n:Valeriu Strelet: Valeriu Strelet was prime minister of Moldova, based in Chisinau. Dorin Dragutanu announced his resignation as governor of the National Bank of Moldova after criticism that he had failed to prevent about one billion US dollars disappearing from three Moldovan banks in 2014. He said he was resigning because of pressure from some politicians, and denied responsibility, saying he had repeatedly warned the authorities. President Nicolae Timofti and Strelet had both said he should be removed.
n:Zhogorku Kenesh: The Zhogorku Kenesh is the parliament of Kyrgyzstan, in Bishkek. Melis Turgunbaev, chairman of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic since 26 June 2024, submitted a letter of resignation, and Speaker Marlen Mamataliev announced it in a session of the parliament. It was described as a voluntary resignation.
n:Anti-Corruption Commission of the Mald: The Anti-Corruption Commission of the Maldives is the country's anti-corruption body, in Male. A report it published in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent over the embezzlement of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation: the bank's Financial Intelligence Unit, which is meant to spot suspicious money, was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque to a firm called SOF but did not investigate it properly or pass the case on. In March 2019 police confirmed that governor Ahmed Naseer was under investigation for obstruction of justice, which is unproven.
n:Banco Orienta: Banco Orienta was a private bank in Paraguay that the Central Bank of Paraguay took over and declared bankrupt. On 6 June 2006 a court in Asuncion sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from Orienta and another private bank, Union. Jose Pecci, a former superintendent at the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor had asked for ten years.
n:Berkshire Hills Bancorp: Berkshire Hills Bancorp is a banking company in Boston. Eric S. Rosengren, president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston from 2007 until he retired in 2021, joined the boards of Berkshire Hills Bancorp and Berkshire Bank with effect from 5 April 2023. The company announced the appointment in April 2023.
n:Centro para Democracia e Desenvolvimen: The Centro para Democracia e Desenvolvimento, in Maputo, followed Mozambique's hidden-debts trial day by day. On the 49th day, 23 November 2021, Bank of Mozambique administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that the central bank should not have authorised the loans to ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose payout depends on a state guarantee. She said governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and keep technical staff out, as the file concerned state security. ProIndicus was approved 372 million US dollars in March 2013 and EMATUM 850 million that August.
n:D. E. Shaw group: The D. E. Shaw group is a hedge fund manager in New York. Brian Sack, who ran the New York Federal Reserve's Markets Group from mid-2009 to 2012 and had earlier spent six years at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, joined the firm's macro investing unit as senior vice president and co-director of global economics. Angel Ubide, a former staff economist at the International Monetary Fund, took the same title. The firm announced both hires.
n:Eurostandard Bank: Eurostandard Bank was a commercial bank in North Macedonia that was put under administration, meaning the central bank took over running it. An association of its depositors said in a press release that the governor tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out first, and that financial police reports were kept secret so the bank could keep operating. It said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months beforehand and that over 60 million euros were lost. No charges and no official finding are reported.
n:Government of Bolivia: This is the national government in La Paz. The Central Bank of Bolivia dismissed more than a dozen of its senior managers, among them the manager for international operations, the principal adviser on political economy and subdirectors of several departments. A former governor of the bank said the dismissals were likely influenced by the change of government. The governor himself was not removed.
n:KPMG Auditores Independentes: KPMG Auditores Independentes is an accounting firm in Sao Paulo. It audited the accounts of the Central Bank of Brazil for the financial year that ended on 31 December 2018. An audit is an outside check that the figures an institution publishes are accurate.
n:Maldives Police Service: The Maldives Police Service is the national police force, based in Male. In March 2019 it summoned Ahmed Naseer, governor of the Maldives Monetary Authority, and confirmed he was being investigated for obstruction of justice. Parliament's Financial Committee had questioned him on 5 March about the Anti-Corruption Commission's report on the embezzlement case at the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation, and about the removal of Abdulla Ashraf as head of the Financial Intelligence Unit. The investigation is unproven.
n:Members of the Jordanian Parliament: These are elected members of Jordan's parliament in Amman. In September 2003 some of them signed a petition urging Prime Minister Ali Abulragheb to remove Umayya Touqan, governor of the Central Bank of Jordan, after Touqan froze all the bank accounts belonging to six leaders of Hamas. The petition was a demand to the prime minister, not a legal step against the governor.
n:National Assembly of Serbia: The National Assembly of Serbia is the country's parliament, in Belgrade. It passed a law giving members of parliament the power to nominate and appoint the top officials of the National Bank of Serbia. Governor Mladjan Dinkic said the law undermined the bank's independence and resigned, as did two of its three deputy governors. Energy Minister Kori Udovicki was nominated to replace him.
n:Office of the Auditor General of Thail: The Office of the Auditor General of Thailand, also called the State Audit Office, is the government body in Bangkok that checks public accounts. It audits the Bank of Thailand and signed the auditor's report on its financial statements for the year that ended on 31 December 2025. An audit is a check that published figures are accurate.
n:Proindicus: Proindicus is a Mozambican company at the centre of the hidden-debts case, in which state-backed loans of more than two billion US dollars were taken from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, in the trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he signed the authorisations for the loans to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed personally to senior officials rather than submitted at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. The law bars the bank from authorising such loans when repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove said that applied only to guarantees obtained afterwards, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his reading.
n:SOF Pvt Ltd: SOF Pvt Ltd is a company in the Maldives. An Anti-Corruption Commission report published in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent in the case in which 1.3 billion rufiyaa was embezzled from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. The bank's Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque from that corporation to SOF but did not investigate it properly, did not examine SOF's large transactions through Bank of Maldives and Bank of Ceylon, and did not forward suspected money-laundering cases.
n:State Tribunal of Poland: The State Tribunal is the court in Warsaw that tries senior Polish officials for breaking the law in office. In March 2024 members of parliament from the ruling coalition filed a motion to bring Adam Glapinski, president of the National Bank of Poland, before it on eight charges, among them bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and unauthorised currency interventions. The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses him of indirectly financing the deficit through asset purchases in 2020 and 2021 and of acting without proper authorisation from the Monetary Policy Council for those purchases and for foreign-exchange interventions. Glapinski and the bank called the allegations baseless, and no vote had taken place. Nothing has been proven.
n:TBC Bank: TBC Bank is a commercial bank in Tbilisi. It and Bank of Georgia had frozen the accounts of Otar Partskhaladze. At a briefing on 20 September 2023, the acting president of the National Bank of Georgia, Natia Turnava, confirmed she had single-handedly changed the procedure for carrying out sanctions regimes, deciding on 19 September with effect from the next day. She said it was within her discretion, that she had told National Bank Council members beforehand, and that the two banks broke no law because the change took effect the day of her briefing. Vice-president Papuna Lezhava resigned.
n:Virabongsa Ramangkura: Virabongsa Ramangkura was chairman of the Bank of Thailand, in Bangkok. During a dispute between the bank and Finance Minister Kittiratt Na-Ranong, he pointed to the cabinet's power under Section 28/19 of the Bank of Thailand Act to remove the governor, who was then Prasarn Trairatvorakul. He stopped short of directly calling for the governor to be removed.
n:i(x) investments: i(x) investments is an investment company in New York. Sarah Bloom Raskin, who had been a governor of the Federal Reserve Board and then Deputy Secretary of the Treasury, was named to its board of directors in an announcement dated 10 August 2017.
n:Antonio Carlos do Rosario: Antonio Carlos do Rosario is named in a documented case in Mozambique involving the Bank of Mozambique, the country's central bank. On 23 November 2021, the 49th day of the hidden-debts trial, bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that the central bank should not have authorised the ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM loans, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose disbursement depends on a state guarantee. She said then governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and keep technical staff out.
n:CL Financial: CL Financial was a company in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, whose collapse was examined by a commission of enquiry set up in November 2010 under sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman. It found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers over the insurance industry fundamentally deficient, tracing that to the narrow scope of the Insurance Act, and said Clico and CL Financial management largely ignored the limited tools the Inspector of financial institutions did have. It blamed no named central bank official.
n:Commission of Enquiry into CL Financia: This inquiry in Trinidad and Tobago examined the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union. Sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman sat from March 2011 to May 2013, at a cost of 36.2 million dollars. He found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers over insurance fundamentally deficient, and blamed no named official. On 6 December 2012 Queen's Counsel Peter Carter put it to former governor Ewart Williams that intervening in 2006 would have spared over 10 billion Trinidad and Tobago dollars; that was cross-examination, not a finding.
