Chen Szu-kuan (陳思寬) is a director of the 21st Board of Directors of the Central Bank of the Republic of China, for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030, while serving as chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited and chairman of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited. Holding both roles at once is a tie, not a finding of wrongdoing.
n:BDO Austria GmbH Wirtschaftsprufungs-: BDO Austria GmbH Wirtschaftsprufungs- und Steuerberatungsgesellschaft is an accounting firm in Austria. It is the outside auditor of the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria's central bank, meaning it checks the bank's accounts from outside the institution. Its approved term runs from 2023 to 2027, set under the European Union Council decision that names the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Banknote Paper Mill (Malyn): The Banknote Paper Mill at Malyn, in Ukraine, makes the paper that Ukraine's hryvnia banknotes are printed on, supplying the National Bank of Ukraine. The bank's own account of the currency, given by Vasyl Ishchenko, places the paper's making at Malyn and describes the notes as carrying sophisticated security features and lasting well in circulation.
n:Crown Agents Investment Management: Crown Agents Investment Management is a money manager based in London, tied to five central banks, and in each case it runs money rather than only advising. Three of the five mandates are over the country's allocation of special drawing rights, the reserve asset the International Monetary Fund issues: it manages about 95 per cent of the Central Bank of the Solomon Islands' allocation, it manages the Bank of Jamaica's, which began at 250 million US dollars and has since doubled with the bank giving the firm discretion over how to invest it, and it took on the Central Bank of Eswatini's SDR-based portfolio in October 2023 after the bank had tried managing it internally. For the Central Bank of Seychelles it runs a fixed income portfolio split evenly between US dollars and Chinese renminbi, begun in 2014 with 25.0 million US dollars and topped up by another 25.0 million in April 2022. For the Reserve Bank of Malawi it appears in the bank's own audited statements for 2025 as the external fund manager behind 3,880 million kwacha of foreign reserves, listed in the counterparty table as Crown Agents Fund manager of the United Kingdom and separately from the bank's three banking lines with Crown Agents Bank Limited. Alongside the Eswatini and Solomon Islands mandates it also trains the banks' own staff, through regular calls, visits and workshops in the first case and online training on investment reporting in the second. Three of these five records come from a trade-press award profile rather than from a bank document, and say so.
Ernst & Young d.o.o. is an accounting firm in Croatia. It is the outside auditor of the Croatian National Bank, the body that checks the central bank's accounts from outside it, for the financial years 2025 to 2027. The appointment was made by the Council of the European Union, which amended its 1999 decision naming the external auditors of national central banks to record it.
n:Hungarian Banknote Printing Company: The Hungarian Banknote Printing Company, in Budapest, prints the forint notes that Hungarians carry. The Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Hungary's central bank, says the printer is an enterprise it owns outright, so the bank that issues the money also owns the works that makes it.
n:Mazars Niger: Mazars Niger is an accounting firm in Niger. It was selected to audit the accounts of the Central Bank of West African States, known by its French initials BCEAO, which issues the shared currency of a group of West African countries. Its term covers the financial years 2024 to 2029, and the selection was announced by the BCEAO itself.
n:Perum Peruri: Perum Peruri, in Jakarta, is described as Indonesia's state banknote printing firm. Bank Indonesia, the central bank, gave it the job of printing the country's new banknotes, and the work was done at Peruri's plant at Karawang in West Java. Peruri denied that a private firm in Central Java had printed any of the notes.
n:South African Bank Note Company: The South African Bank Note Company, formally the South African Bank Note Company (RF) Proprietary Limited, is in Pretoria and prints South Africa's banknotes. The South African Reserve Bank, the country's central bank, says the printer is one of its own subsidiaries, so the bank that issues the money owns the company that produces it.
Valora S.A., at Carregado in Portugal, is the banknote printer owned by the Banco de Portugal, and it prints notes for that central bank. A Banque de France press release names it as the bank's printer. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:BNP Paribas Asset Management: BNP Paribas Asset Management is a firm based in Paris, France. Chile's Ministry of Finance says it is the sole outside manager of the US agency mortgage-backed securities portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, the state's savings pots, and that the Banco Central de Chile runs the selection of outside managers, handles the sovereign fixed income share of the funds itself, and supervises outside managers holding instruments that qualify for the country's international reserves. This is management of money, not advice.
n:Mellon Investments Corporation: Mellon Investments Corporation is a firm based in Boston, United States. Chile's Ministry of Finance says it manages part of the share portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, the state's savings pots. The Banco Central de Chile runs the process that picks these outside managers and supervises those holding instruments that qualify for the country's international reserves. Mellon is handling money, not giving advice.
n:Banknote Printing and Minting Works of: The Banknote Printing and Minting Works of the National Bank of Ukraine is a state printing works in Kyiv. It prints the hryvnia, Ukraine's banknotes, and the National Bank of Ukraine says the works is part of the bank itself. So the country's cash is made in-house rather than ordered from an outside printer.
n:De La Rue Lanka Currency and Security: De La Rue Lanka Currency and Security Print (Pvt) Ltd is a firm at Biyagama, Sri Lanka. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka says in its own question-and-answer page on currency that this company prints the country's currency notes at Biyagama. The job of making a country's cash therefore sits with a company outside the central bank.
Grant Thornton Audit, s.r.o. is a firm in Slovakia. It checks the books of the National Bank of Slovakia as that bank's outside auditor, an appointment approved for the financial years 2024 to 2027 under the European Union decision that names the external auditors of the national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Imprenta de Billetes S.A. (IMBISA): Imprenta de Billetes S.A., known as IMBISA, is a state printing works in Madrid, Spain, 80 per cent owned by the Banco de España. It prints the euro banknotes allotted to Spain, which the Banco de España puts at roughly 12 per cent of all euro banknote production, so the Spanish central bank owns most of the plant that makes a sizeable share of the shared currency's cash.
n:PriceWaterhouseCoopers & Associados -: PriceWaterhouseCoopers & Associados - Sociedade de Revisores Oficiais de Contas Lda is a firm in Portugal. It checks the books of the Bank of Portugal as that bank's outside auditor, an appointment approved for the financial years 2022 to 2026 under the European Union decision naming the external auditors of the national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Tribunal de Cuentas: The Tribunal de Cuentas is a state body in Montevideo, Uruguay. It checks the books of the Central Bank of Uruguay. That duty is not a contract the bank can end but a standing requirement written into the bank's founding law, Ley 16.696 of 1995, which remains in force, so the auditing is done by the state itself rather than by a hired accounting firm.
n:World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory a: The Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, RAMP, is run by the World Bank's treasury department in Washington, DC, and offers member central banks three things: advice, training for senior staff, and the actual handling of money. It is tied to 25 central banks, and what each gets differs. Guatemala, Trinidad and Tobago, Cambodia and Bulgaria are listed only as members, Bulgaria also co-hosting a RAMP forum. Ecuador, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cabo Verde, Liberia, Libya, Zimbabwe, Somalia, Georgia, El Salvador and the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank signed up for advice, technical assistance or capacity building. Armenia rejoined for advice and training, after membership from 2006 to 2014. Paraguay joined in 2017 and used RAMP advice to rewrite its own investment policy, still running its reserves itself. In nine places the banks' own documents say RAMP handles money rather than advising on it: Seychelles, where a portfolio of international reserves was first funded with 100 million US dollars in 2019 and still held at the end of 2025; Kosovo, which signed a new membership agreement on 16 April 2026 under which a portion of its reserves will be managed; Moldova, Kenya, Tanzania, Romania and Mongolia, each from a line in their audited accounts; the BCEAO, which holds units in a RAMP fund the World Bank manages; and Lesotho, whose Central Bank statements put 1,932,669 thousand maloti of its reserves under RAMP management at 31 December 2025.
n:Baker Tilly Klitou and Partners Limite: Baker Tilly Klitou and Partners Limited is a private firm in Cyprus. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts. Its approved term runs from 2023 to 2027, set out in a Council of the European Union decision amending Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, document 11852/24. That is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Deloitte Audit Ltd: Deloitte Audit Ltd is a private firm in Malta. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Malta, the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts, under an approved term covering 2023 to 2027. That term was set by Council Decision (EU) 2023/1196 of 16 June 2023, published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Grant Thornton Ireland: Grant Thornton Ireland is a private firm in Ireland. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Ireland, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books rather than bank staff doing it themselves. Its approved term covers 2023 to 2027, recorded in the consolidated text of Council Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024. That is the only central bank tied to the firm.
KPMG Audit S.a r.l. is a private firm in Luxembourg. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Luxembourg, the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts. Its approved term runs from 2024 to 2028, set by Council Decision (EU) 2024/864 of 12 March 2024, published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicher: Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicherheitsdruck GmbH, or OeBS, is a state printing works in Vienna, Austria. It prints the banknotes for the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria's central bank, which owns it. A joint press release from the Banque de France names OeBS as one of three printers owned by central banks that are strengthening their cooperation on banknote production. Austria's central bank is the only one tied to it.
n:Security Printing Corporation (Banglad: The Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) Ltd is a state printing works in Gazipur, Bangladesh. It prints the banknotes for Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank. The Business Standard reports that Bangladesh's taka notes are printed there, at a site known locally as Takshal that covers about 66 acres and has been in operation since 1989. Bangladesh Bank is the only central bank tied to it.
n:UAB ROSK Consulting: UAB ROSK Consulting is a private firm in Lithuania. It is the external auditor of the Bank of Lithuania, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books, under an approved term covering 2022 to 2024. That term is set out in the consolidated text of Council Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
Baker Tilly Nicaragua, S.A. is a private firm based in Managua, Nicaragua. It acts as the outside auditor of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside the bank and reports on whether the figures hold up. Its work appears in the central bank's financial statements for 2024, published by the Banco Central de Nicaragua.
n:Corte de Cuentas de la Republica: The Corte de Cuentas de la Republica is a state body in San Salvador, El Salvador. It audits the accounts of the Central Reserve Bank of El Salvador, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. This is not a contract with an end date but a duty written into the law that governs the central bank, and that law is in force.
n:Diósgyőr Papermill: The Diósgyőr Papermill in Miskolc, Hungary, is a state printing works and a wholly owned subsidiary of the Hungarian Banknote Printing Company. It does not print money itself; it makes the special paper the notes are printed on. The Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Hungary's central bank, states that the paper for forint banknotes is made at this mill.
n:Horwath Central America: Horwath Central America is a private firm in Honduras. It is the outside auditor of the Central Bank of Honduras, checking the bank's books and reporting on them rather than keeping them. It audited the central bank's financial statements as at 31 December 2023, which were published through Honduras's single transparency portal.
n:KPMG Bedrijfsrevisoren / KPMG Reviseur: KPMG Bedrijfsrevisoren / KPMG Reviseurs d'Entreprises BV/SRL is a private firm in Belgium. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of Belgium, that is, it checks the bank's books from outside and reports on them. The appointment covers the years 2023 to 2028 and is recorded in a Council decision of the European Union on the outside auditors of national central banks.
n:Security Printing and Minting Organiza: The Security Printing and Minting Organization, in Tehran, is a state printing works and has been a subsidiary of the Central Bank of Iran since 1962. It handles the design, production and destruction of Iran's banknotes and coins. Until 1982 Iran's banknotes were printed abroad; since then they have come from this organization.
n:UBS Asset Management: UBS Asset Management is a private firm based in Zurich, Switzerland, and it handles money for two central banks. For the Central Bank of Seychelles it runs a money market fund holding part of the country's reserves, funded with 10.0 million US dollars in 2017 and still held at the end of 2025, and it has invited bank staff to its annual reserves management seminar. For Chile, UBS Asset Management Inc manages part of the corporate bond portfolio and part of the equity portfolio of the sovereign wealth funds, with the Banco Central de Chile selecting and supervising the outside managers.
n:\"Ernst&Young Montenegro\" Ltd Podgori: "Ernst&Young Montenegro" Ltd Podgorica is a firm based in Podgorica, Montenegro. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Montenegro, meaning it checks from outside that the bank's books are accurate. Its most recent audit covered the 2025 accounts, as recorded in the central bank's summary of its audit committee report for that year.
n:Davlat Belgisi: Davlat Belgisi is a state printing operation in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, and it prints the banknotes of the Central Bank of Uzbekistan. The central bank lists it among its own subordinate organisations, as a state production association set up as a limited liability company under the bank and made up of the Tashkent Printing Factory, the Tashkent Paper Factory and the Tashkent Mint. Its core business is given as making banknote and other security papers, banknotes and passports.
n:Northern Trust: Northern Trust is a bank and asset servicing firm based in Chicago, United States. Its 2025 annual report shows an average holding of 70 million US dollars of Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago stock; at the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors, and since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. J. Charles Partee came from the Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Federal Reserve's staff and then a governorship from 5 January 1976 to 7 February 1986, and afterwards joined the board of State Farm Insurance and a mutual fund trusteeship. For the Bank of Botswana, Central Banking's global custodian award profile says Northern Trust provides performance measurement and attribution reporting and runs training for bank staff on benchmark construction and fixed-income investment. For the Bank of Uganda it provides compliance, performance and risk sensitivity analysis, helped build a dashboard for overseeing the bank's external asset managers alongside monthly audited reports, and supported a redesign of the bank's strategic asset allocation system. In both cases the profile describes services, training and advice rather than managing the money.
n:State Street Global Advisors: State Street Global Advisors is a firm based in Boston, United States, and it manages money for one central bank. Central Banking's award profile reports that it holds a mandate to invest shares for the Czech National Bank, raised to 7.5 billion US dollars, and that the Czech bank's executive director of risk management says it has kept that mandate with the firm since 2007. The firm also gives the bank its views when it weighs alternatives to its current approach to reserves.
n:Amundi: Amundi is a firm based in Paris, France, tied to six central banks. In 2023 the Bank of the Republic (Colombia) chose it as one of eight outside managers, and it runs an active fixed income programme covering 1.7 billion US dollars of Treasuries, mortgage-backed securities and G10 currencies. The Central Bank of Bolivia names it as one of three delegated managers of the Fondo RAL-ME, the foreign-currency reserve Bolivian banks must hold at the central bank, which stood at 1,052 million US dollars at the end of 2018; the same report records three compliance breaches by Amundi in 2018, two trades through a broker that had not been approved and one breach of the limit on exposure to a single bank. The National Bank of Kazakhstan's consolidated financial statements for 2012 name it as one of six foreign asset management organisations given part of the international reserves that year, with 92,171,780 thousand tenge under its management in global shares against the MSCI World index, the largest of the six; the bank's later reports say external managers are used and name none, so that figure is a 2012 position rather than a current one. The Central Bank of Ireland appointed it to run the bank's own portfolio of equities under a tender numbered 2016P038, on a contract worth 700,000 euro excluding value added tax. With the Latin American Reserve Fund it also built a fixed-income exchange-traded fund for central banks, a pooled product rather than a mandate to run reserves; the Central Bank of Uruguay and the Bank of Mexico are named as clients.
n:Ernst & Young Statutory Auditors, Bran: Ernst & Young Statutory Auditors, Branch in Albania is a firm based in Tirana, Albania. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Bank of Albania, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside and signs off on them. The Bank of Albania's own financial statements record it as the auditor for 2023.
n:Sudanese Company for Currency Printing: The Sudanese Company for Currency Printing is a printing works in Khartoum, Sudan, tied to one central bank. It prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Sudan. Dabanga reported in February 2019 that Sudan's new 200-pound note went into production there, at a domestic press the prime minister visited that week. Who owns the company is not stated.
n:BDO Assurance NV: BDO Assurance NV is a firm in Suriname that audits accounts, meaning it checks another organisation's books and says whether the figures are right. One central bank is tied to it: it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Suriname. The audit on record covers that bank's 2020 accounts, published in its annual financial statements for that year.
n:KPMG Moldova SRL: KPMG Moldova SRL is a firm in Moldova that audits accounts, meaning it examines another organisation's books and states whether the figures are right. One central bank is tied to it: it audits the accounts of the National Bank of Moldova. The audits on record cover 2024 and 2023, as set out in that bank's financial statements for 2024.
n:Oumolat Security Printing: Oumolat Security Printing is a banknote printer in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates. Currency News reported on 31 March 2025 that the Central Bank of the UAE had issued a new 100 dirham polymer banknote printed by Oumolat. A 2023 profile in the same publication says the firm began operations in 2016, was owned and started by the Emirates Investment Authority, and was then transferred to the Central Bank of the UAE, so the bank whose money it prints is also its owner.
n:West African Monetary Institute: The West African Monetary Institute is an international body in Accra, Ghana. It manages a shared fund that one central bank, the Bank of Sierra Leone, pays into. That bank's audited financial statements for 2024 list its contribution to the Stabilization and Cooperation Fund, 63.59 million leones, among its foreign assets, and say the institute manages the fund, with the balance held at the Bank of Ghana. What it runs is the pooled fund, not the central bank's own reserves.
n:DWS Group: DWS Group is a firm based in Frankfurt, Germany. It is one of the outside managers that invest part of the foreign reserves of the Bank of Papua New Guinea on the bank's behalf, measured against the FTSE Russell Government Bond Index 1-3 Years USD Hedged. The bank's Annual Report 2024 says DWS and BlackRock delivered the strongest results for the year, while Pictet recorded the weakest relative performance.
n:Pictet Asset Management: Pictet Asset Management is a firm based in Geneva, Switzerland. It is one of the outside managers that invest part of the foreign reserves of the Bank of Papua New Guinea on the bank's behalf, measured against the FTSE Russell Government Bond Index 1-3 Years USD Hedged. In the bank's Annual Report 2024, Pictet recorded the weakest relative performance for the year, while DWS and BlackRock delivered the strongest results.
n:Latin American Reserve Fund (FLAR): The Latin American Reserve Fund, known as FLAR, is an international body based in Bogota, Colombia. Central Banking's announcement of its 2026 awards gave the partner initiative award to Amundi and FLAR for a fixed-income exchange-traded fund they developed together for central banks, built around environmental, social and governance standards, and named the Central Bank of Uruguay and the Bank of Mexico among the clients. This is a fund those banks put money into, not a mandate to manage their reserves.
n:Statni tiskarna cenin: Statni tiskarna cenin is a state printing works in Prague, Czechia, tied to one central bank, the Czech National Bank. It printed some of that bank's banknotes: the bank says the reverse of its commemorative note marking the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency carries, in tiny letters near the lower edge, the inscription "STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA". No printing date is given; the note was issued in 2022 and entered circulation on 30 March 2022. Who prints the bank's circulating notes is not stated.
n:Auditor General of the Cayman Islands: The Auditor General of the Cayman Islands, Patrick O. Smith, a certified public accountant and certified fraud examiner, heads the government audit office there. The office is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, and its audit for 2025 appears in that authority's annual report, tabled in the Cayman Islands Parliament.
n:Moteane, Quashie & Associates and Sizw: Moteane, Quashie & Associates and SizweNtsalubaGobodo Grant Thornton Inc. are accounting firms working together from Maseru, Lesotho. They are tied to one central bank: they audit the accounts of the Central Bank of Lesotho, and signed its annual financial statements for the year ended 2023.
n:Deloitte Namibia and Grand Namibia: Deloitte Namibia and Grand Namibia are accounting firms based in Windhoek, Namibia. They are tied to one central bank: they are the external auditors of the Bank of Namibia and audit its accounts.
n:Hong Kong Note Printing Limited: Hong Kong Note Printing Limited is a firm in Hong Kong that prints banknotes. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's page on Hong Kong notes says the notes issued by the note-issuing banks are printed in Hong Kong by the company. The same page says the government keeps management control and a majority stake in it, with the chief executive of the Monetary Authority as the company's chairman. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Bureau of Engraving and Printing: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing is a United States government works that prints banknotes for the Federal Reserve System, the country's central bank. Its own About page says it prints billions of dollars each year, in notes called Federal Reserve notes. The page gives no location for the agency, so it is marked at the country rather than at the office. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea (A: The Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea, also called the Auditor General's Office, is based in Port Moresby. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Papua New Guinea, the country's central bank, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside. The tie is recorded for 2024, from the central bank's annual report for that year. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Auditor General (of Nepal): The Auditor General of Nepal, based in Kathmandu, audits the accounts of Nepal Rastra Bank, the country's central bank: it checks the bank's books from outside the bank. The duty comes from section 92 of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, dated 2002 in the numbering used there. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:World Bank Treasury: The World Bank Treasury is based in Washington, D.C., in the United States, and one central bank is tied to it. Financial Afrik reports that the governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, Sid'Ahmed Ould Raiss, and the World Bank's vice-president and treasurer Madelyn Antoncic signed a cooperation agreement on foreign exchange reserve management at the IMF-World Bank spring meetings, under which the treasury department would train reserve staff, organise the relevant structures and eventually set up a trading room. That is technical assistance, not management of the money itself.
n:Auditor General of Seychelles, audit r: The Auditor General of Seychelles, in Victoria, Seychelles, audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Seychelles, the one central bank tied to it, with the audit review carried out by Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited in Abu Dhabi. Auditing means checking the bank's books and reporting whether they give an accurate picture. The audit covers 2025 and appears in the central bank's annual report for that year, which was tabled in the National Assembly.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbe: PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbean is an accounting firm at Bird Rock in Basseterre, St. Kitts & Nevis. It audits the accounts of the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, the one central bank tied to it, which means it checks the bank's books and reports whether they give an accurate picture. The audit covers 2025 and is published with the central bank's financial statements as an independent auditors' report.

n:Groupement PKF BAGE SARL et CROWE TG I: This is a pair of audit firms based in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, appointed together in 2023 to check the accounts of the Burkina Faso arm of the Central Bank of West African States. n:Deloitte & Touche, Certified Public Ac: Deloitte & Touche, certified public accountants, is based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. n:GRANT THORNTON SENEGAL (titulaire), Gr: A pair of accounting firms in Dakar, Senegal, appointed together: Grant Thornton Senegal as titulaire, the firm that does the audit, and a grouping of PKF BAGE SARL and Crowe TG ICAAF as suppléant, the stand-in. n:Auditor General's Office: The Auditor General's Office in Honiara is the Solomon Islands' own public auditor. n:Bank of Canada: The Bank of Canada is Canada's central bank, in Ottawa, and two other central banks keep gold in its vaults. n:Oesterreichische Nationalbank: The Oesterreichische Nationalbank is Austria's central bank, in Vienna. It shares the management of some reserves with Latvia's central bank, Latvijas Banka. n:Sveriges Riksbank: Sveriges Riksbank is Sweden's central bank, in Stockholm. One other central bank keeps gold with it. n:KPMG Armenia LLC: KPMG Armenia LLC is an accounting firm based in Yerevan, Armenia. n:Swiss National Bank: The Swiss National Bank is Switzerland's central bank, based in Bern. Two other central banks store gold with it, which is custody rather than management of their money. n:Castillo Sanchez & Burrell, LLP, Chart: Castillo Sanchez & Burrell, LLP, Chartered Accountants is a firm of chartered accountants in Belize. n:KPMG Audit SRL: KPMG Audit SRL is an accounting firm based in Bucharest, Romania. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of Romania, Romania's central bank, and did so for that bank's 2019 annual report. No other central bank is tied to it.

n:Banque de France: The Banque de France is France's central bank, based in Paris. One central bank is tied to it here: it stores gold belonging to the Deutsche Bundesbank, Germany's central bank. n:KPMG Audit Azerbaijan LLC: KPMG Audit Azerbaijan LLC is an accounting firm based in Baku, Azerbaijan. n:Gaveglio Aparicio y Asociados Sociedad: Gaveglio Aparicio y Asociados Sociedad Civil de Responsabilidad Limitada is an accounting firm in Lima, Peru, and a member firm of PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited. n:Royal Canadian Mint: The Royal Canadian Mint is a state body in Ottawa, Canada. n:Banca d'Italia: Banca d'Italia is Italy's central bank, based in Rome. The one tie recorded for it is to itself: it stores its own gold. n:PKF Gambia and PKF Nigeria: PKF Gambia and PKF Nigeria is an accountancy firm based in Bijilo, Gambia. n:Central Asian Secure Printing Typograp: Central Asian Secure Printing Typography LLC is a banknote printing firm in Kyrgyzstan. n:BDO T&T: BDO T&T is an accounting firm in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, the country's central bank, and did so for 2024. n:KPMG Georgia LLC: KPMG Georgia LLC is an accounting and auditing firm based in Tbilisi, Georgia. It audited the accounts of the National Bank of Georgia for the year ended 31 December 2020. n:Deloitte & Touche with BDO (joint audi: This is a joint appointment of two accounting firms, Deloitte & Touche and BDO, auditing together as one engagement. n:Ernst & Young Chartered Accountants: Ernst & Young Chartered Accountants is the Jamaican practice of the accounting and auditing firm Ernst & Young, at 8 Olivier Road, Kingston 8. n:KPMG Afrique Centrale with Mazars Came: This is a joint appointment of two accounting firms, KPMG Afrique Centrale and Mazars Cameroun, auditing together as the commissaires aux comptes of the Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale, the central bank shared by Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, Congo-Brazzaville, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. n:KPMG Fakhro: KPMG Fakhro is the Bahraini practice of the accounting and auditing firm KPMG, at the 12th floor of Fakhro Tower in Manama. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Bahrain. n:SNG Grant Thornton Chartered Accountan: SNG Grant Thornton Chartered Accountants (Eswatini) is an accounting firm at Lot 195 Kal Grant Street, Mbabane, and part of the Grant Thornton network. n:Forvis Mazars Cameroun SA: Forvis Mazars Cameroun SA is the Cameroonian practice of the accounting and auditing firm Forvis Mazars. It audits the accounts of the Bank of the Republic of Burundi. n:Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN, Char: Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN are two firms of chartered accountants in Dhaka that audit Bangladesh Bank's accounts together, each signing the same report. n:KPMG S.A. and Merove-Pierre - Cabinet: KPMG S.A., the French firm in the KPMG network, and Merove-Pierre - Cabinet d'Experts-Comptables, an accounting firm at 7 rue Lechaud, Bourdon, Port-au-Prince, audit the accounts of the Bank of the Republic of Haiti together. n:Ernst & Young RDC: Ernst & Young RDC is the Congolese practice of the accounting and auditing firm Ernst & Young, at Immeuble Onze Treize, 110 Boulevard du 30 juin, Gombe, Kinshasa. The governor's own foreword to the same annual report states that the bank's accounts were audited and certified without reserve by the firm.
n:Gemcorp Capital: Gemcorp Capital is a firm in London that invests money for others. It manages part of the National Bank of Angola's foreign reserves, and by the end of 2023 it held 56 percent of them: 601,697 million kwanzas, about 725 million US dollars, up from 286,532 million kwanzas a year earlier. The money sits in three holdings named in the central bank's accounts: a stake in Gemcorp Fund Limited, set up in 2017 and worth 492,786 million kwanzas at the end of 2023; 133.89 million dollars put in 2023 into a vehicle called L-Crest, worth 131.40 million dollars at the end of that year; and 108,911 million kwanzas in a fund holding public and corporate debt. For the 2019 and 2020 accounts the firm did not tell the central bank what it had invested the money in, which under international accounting rules obliged the bank to write the holding down to nothing; the bank renewed the investment for a further six years. Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, asked about the L-Crest holding, said it was a portfolio of government bonds and that the 2.49 million dollar shortfall was on paper rather than realised, and referred to the central bank's other external managers, who are not named. Gemcorp is also described as one of the bank's largest creditors, so it lends to the institution whose reserves it invests.
n:KPMG Baltics OÜ: KPMG Baltics OÜ is an accounting firm in Estonia. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Estonia, known in Estonian as Eesti Pank, as its external auditor, the outside firm that checks the bank's accounts rather than its own staff doing so. It holds that role for the financial years 2026 to 2030. The appointment runs through Council Decision (EU) 2026/443 of 17 February 2026: in the euro area the external auditor of each national central bank is recommended by the European Central Bank and then approved by the Council of the European Union, so the firm is chosen by the bank but confirmed in law.
n:KPMG Baltics SIA: KPMG Baltics SIA is an accounting firm in Latvia. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Latvia, known in Latvian as Latvijas Banka, as its external auditor, the outside firm that checks the bank's accounts rather than its own staff doing so. It holds that role for the financial years 2025 to 2029, under the Council Decision of 27 May 2025. As with every euro-area central bank, the auditor is recommended by the European Central Bank and approved by the Council of the European Union.
n:Central Bank of West African States he: The head office of the Central Bank of West African States, in Dakar, keeps part of the union's gold itself. Note 6 of the bank's financial statements for 2024 lists gold held at the head office as one of three locations, at 199,368 million CFA francs; Agence Ecofin, reading the same statements, says only about 120,000 ounces are physically stored there, under 8 per cent of the total. The other two of the three locations are outside the continent. The gold belongs to the union as a whole: it is pooled at the BCEAO rather than apportioned among the eight member countries.
n:Government of France: France designates seats on the board of the Central Bank of the Comoros: two of the six members, alongside the governor and three administrators designated by the Comorian government. Two French-designated members also sit on the committee that sets monetary policy and manages the reserves, whose other members are the governor and one person designated by the Comorian government, and two sit on the banking supervision committee. The balance used to be even. Under the statutes published by Legifrance in 2010 the board had up to eight members, half named by each government; new statutes signed in Paris on 3 December 2024, in force since March 2025, cut the French share while keeping French seats on the bodies that decide. The arrangement is not hidden: it is set out in the bank's own organisation chart.
n:French Treasury (Direction generale du: The French Treasury still holds part of BEAC's foreign exchange reserves. Its own page on how the Franc Zone works says the BEAC must deposit at least 50 per cent of the CEMAC zone's reserves in an operations account opened in the BEAC's name, a share cut from 65 per cent in 2007. That required share earns the European Central Bank's marginal lending facility rate, 0.25 per cent since 16 March 2016. Anything the BEAC chooses to leave above the required share earns the ECB's minimum rate on main refinancing operations, which has been 0 per cent since the same date, so the extra money sits there without earning.
n:Central Bank of Ireland: One country's central bank running another's reserves is rare, and this is a case of it. The Central Bank of Ireland has managed the Central Bank of Malta's share of the European Central Bank's US dollar pooled reserves since 1 January 2008, at Malta's own request. Each euro-area country transferred reserves to the ECB in proportion to its shareholding, and those reserves are managed in a decentralised way by the national central banks, which act for the ECB on a disclosed agency basis; Malta is the one that handed the job to another country's bank. Ireland's and Malta's shares together come to USD 1.5 billion, and Ireland's own portion of the ECB reserves amounted to EUR 0.4 billion.
n:Oesterreichische Nationalbank head off: Austria keeps half its gold at home, and this is where most of that half sits. The Oesterreichische Nationalbank says 140 tons of gold are stored in Austria and 90 tons of it in the bank's own vaults, out of total reserves of 280 tons. The bank puts those 280 tons at some 22,400 gold bars.
n:Danmarks Nationalbank head office, Cop: Almost none of Denmark's gold is in Denmark. Danmarks Nationalbank keeps around 2.5 per cent of its roughly 66.5 tonnes in Copenhagen, and that is the only part held in the country at all. About 97 per cent sits at the Bank of England and about 0.5 per cent at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
n:Narodowy Bank Polski domestic vaults,: Poland brought a large part of its gold home and has not said exactly where it went. A Narodowy Bank Polski publication says the bank moved 100 tons in 2019 from the Bank of England to the domestic vaults, finishing in November that year, and that almost 124 tons were left at the Bank of England. The bank's own text names no building: it says only domestic vaults. A research report on central bank gold repatriation, In Gold We Trust, says the vaults are in Warsaw and Poznan, but that is the report's claim and the bank has not confirmed it.
n:Magyar Nemzeti Bank domestic vaults, H: The Magyar Nemzeti Bank keeps Hungary's gold at home. Its own press release of October 2018 says the stock of gold reserves had already been transported to Hungary, and that the reserves were increased and moved in physical form in the first part of October 2018, taking the holding from 3.1 tons to 31.5 tons, a tenfold rise. Where in Hungary the gold is kept is not stated, so no particular vault or city is claimed here.
n:Banco de Mexico main vault, Mexico Cit: The Bank of Mexico keeps a small part of its gold in its own vault in Mexico City. Its December 2016 answer to a transparency-law request, as reported, puts 1.05 per cent of the gold in Mexico as at the end of October 2016, the rest being abroad. The bank gave no bar or coin count for the gold held at home, unlike the 7,265 bars it listed for the Bank of England. The figures in the article reporting the answer do not add up, which is why what rests on it is marked as a weak source.
n:National Audit Chamber of Sudan: The National Audit Chamber of Sudan is a state body in Khartoum. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Sudan, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. The bank's own annual report presents its balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in owner equity and cash flow statement for the year ended 31 December 2015 as audited by the Chamber. This is not a contract with an end date but a duty written into law: the Central Bank of Sudan Act 2002 requires the accounts to be audited in accordance with the General Audit Chambers Act 1999, naming the statute rather than the auditor, and the bank's report names the body doing the work. One thing worth keeping in view is that the auditor here is part of the same state the bank belongs to, rather than a firm hired from outside it.
n:Grant Thornton DOO: Grant Thornton DOO is an accountancy firm in Skopje, the North Macedonian member of the Grant Thornton international network. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. It signed the Independent Auditor's Report on the bank's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2023, addressed to the bank's Council, and gave an opinion without qualifications. The bank publishes the report on its own website and in the Official Gazette. Grant Thornton is one of the mid-tier networks that sit below the four largest accountancy firms.
n:Fidelity Printers and Refiners: Fidelity Printers and Refiners is a subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, based in Harare. It prints the country's banknotes, which means Zimbabwe's money is made by a company the central bank itself owns rather than bought from an outside printer. Its own corporate history says the work began in 1966 in the basement of the old Reserve Bank building on Samora Machel Avenue, and moved to purpose-built premises at Msasa in 1978-82. In 2021 the printing side was split off into a separate company, the Printing and Minting Company of Zimbabwe. A bank that owns its printer is not unusual and is in some ways the opposite of the risk this map tracks elsewhere, where an outside firm holds the contract; what it does mean is that there is no outside party whose contract terms or payments a reader could examine.
n:Banknote Printing Works of the Nationa: The Banknote Printing Works of the National Bank of Cambodia is the central bank's own printing works. It prints the country's banknotes, so the riel is made in-house rather than ordered from one of the handful of commercial printers that supply most of the world. It is recorded here as the printer of the 200,000-riel note issued on 16 October 2024 for the twentieth anniversary of King Norodom Sihamoni's coronation. As with other state works, there is no outside contract to examine, and what is known here comes from a specialist banknote news service rather than from a document the bank itself publishes.
n:RSM Tajikistan LLC: RSM Tajikistan LLC is an accountancy firm in Dushanbe, the Tajik member of the RSM international network. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of Tajikistan, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. Its managing partner signed the independent auditor's report on the bank's 2023 financial statements, and the firm holds a licence from the National Bank itself to audit banks, which is worth noticing: the body being audited is also the body that licenses its auditor. RSM is one of the mid-tier networks that sit below the four largest accountancy firms. Earlier audits of this bank were done by Deloitte and by Ernst & Young Ford Rhodes Sidat Hyder; this is the current mandate.
n:De Nederlandsche Bank Cash Centre, Zei: The Cash Centre at Zeist is De Nederlandsche Bank's own vault, and it holds the part of the country's gold that is kept at home: 31 per cent of the bank's holding, about 200,000 kilograms. The rest of the holding sits abroad with other institutions. A central bank that keeps gold in its own vault depends on nobody else to reach it, which is the whole point of the choice; the bank is also unusual in publishing the split by location in plain words rather than burying a single line in a note to its accounts.
n:Bank of Mongolia's own vault, Ulaanbaa: This is the Bank of Mongolia's own vault. The bank's audited accounts for 2024 say its monetary gold is held in foreign banks and in the vault of the Bank, so part of the holding is kept at home. The same note no longer says which foreign banks, where earlier accounts named them, so the disclosure has gone backwards rather than forwards. A central bank that keeps gold in its own vault depends on nobody else to reach it.
n:Banque du Liban's own vaults, Beirut: The Banque du Liban keeps roughly two thirds of Lebanon's gold in its own vaults in Beirut, with the rest abroad. The holding, about 287 tonnes, has been unchanged since 1971 and is large for the size of the economy. The bank itself publishes no audited accounts, so none of this comes from it: the split rests on a policy paper by a research institute at the American University of Beirut, and is marked as weakly sourced for that reason.
n:Censorat de la Banque d'Algerie: The Censorat is the body that checks the Bank of Algeria's books. It is not an accountancy firm. Under the money and credit law of 21 June 2023 it is made up of two full-time censeurs appointed by presidential decree, who must have central bank accounting expertise, who verify the end-of-year accounts and report to the bank's board, and who send a report to the Minister of Finance within four months of the year end. There is a fair question, rather than a settled answer, about whether that amounts to an audit from outside the bank, and it is recorded here with the doubt attached: the Censorat is created by the bank's own charter law and its members sit in its board sessions, which is close to arrangements elsewhere that this map treats as having no external auditor at all. It is recorded because the censeurs are put in place by the head of state rather than chosen by the bank, and because they answer to a minister. No private firm is named anywhere in the law for the bank's own accounts.
n:AXIS Capital Holdings Limited: AXIS Capital Holdings Limited is a company based in Pembroke, Bermuda. Its tie to a central bank runs through one person. Cheryl-Ann Lister was Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Bermuda Monetary Authority from 1999 to 2006. On 23 September 2008 AXIS announced that she had joined its board as an independent director, meaning a board member who is not an employee of the company.
n:Accountant General, Government of Beli: The Accountant General, in Belmopan, prepares the financial statements of the Government of Belize. For the 2011/2012 financial year the Auditor General of Belize reported that the Treasury could not show that 25 accounts held at the Central Bank of Belize for the government had been reconciled, that is checked and matched, for the period audited. The same report found that public debt records kept by the central bank did not agree with the Accountant General's statements, and that interest payments it recorded differed from the government's own system.
n:American Bank of Albania: The American Bank of Albania is a bank in Tirana. Gent Sejko, who became Governor of the Bank of Albania and chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015, had held senior executive and committee-chairing posts at the American Bank of Albania earlier in his career, along with similar roles at the National Commercial Bank and Raiffeisen Bank. He moved into the governorship from Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania.
n:Arab African International Bank: The Arab African International Bank is a bank in Cairo. Its link to Egypt's central bank is a career move by one of its own executives. Hassan Abdalla was vice chairman and managing director of the Arab African International Bank, and he left that job to become Governor of the Central Bank of Egypt on 18 August 2022, the post he has held since.
n:Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation: The Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation, or APICORP, is an agency based in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Rasheed Mohammed Al Maraj was its General Manager and Chief Executive Officer, and before that Assistant Under-Secretary at the Ministry of Finance and National Economy and Under-Secretary at the Ministry of Transportation. He left APICORP to become Governor of the Central Bank of Bahrain, a post he has held since January 2005.
n:Arion Bank: Arion Bank is a bank in Reykjavik, the later name of Kaupthing Bank. Asgeir Jonsson was chief economist there and head of its research department. He left that work to become Governor of the Central Bank of Iceland, on a five-year term that began on 20 August 2019. The move was from research in a commercial bank to running the country's central bank.
n:Asian Development Bank: The Asian Development Bank is an international lender based in Manila. Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mongolia from 2007 to 2010 and its representative in London, then went out to work at the Asian Development Bank, among other institutions including the World Bank and the state-owned State Bank of Mongolia, and returned to the Bank of Mongolia as a member of its Supervisory Board in 2025.
n:Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, or AIIB, is an international lender based in Beijing. Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mongolia from 2007 to 2010 and its representative in London, then worked outside it at the AIIB and at other institutions including the World Bank and the state-owned State Bank of Mongolia, before returning to the Bank of Mongolia as a member of its Supervisory Board in 2025.
n:Baker Tilly Moldova: Baker Tilly Moldova is a company in Moldova. Constantin Schendra was its executive director from 2015 to 2018, work he took up after spells as a senior auditor at Ernst & Young. He then crossed into the National Bank of Moldova, running its Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021, and on 4 November 2021 became Deputy Governor and a member of the bank's Executive Committee.
n:Banco AV Villas: Banco AV Villas is a bank in Bogota. Gerardo Hernandez Correa had been a codirector of the Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, as well as its executive manager and the secretary of its Board. He left for the commercial side, becoming vice-president of legal affairs at Banco de Bogota from 2021, and was then named president of Banco AV Villas in an announcement on 27 June 2024.
n:Banco Angolano de Investimentos (BAI): Banco Angolano de Investimentos, or BAI, is a bank in Luanda. Jose de Lima Massano was its chief executive, and an executive director of the state-owned BPC, before becoming Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, Angola's central bank, which he led for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023. He was also elected to BAI's board on 18 August 2015, taking office that 1 September. In June 2023 he left the central bank to become Senior Minister in the President's office.
n:Banco Basa: Banco Basa is a bank in Paraguay. Carlos Fernandez Valdovinos was President of the Banco Central del Paraguay, the country's central bank, from 2013 to 2018. After leaving that post he joined Banco Basa as a member of its board of directors, moving from the head of the institution that oversees the country's money to the board of a commercial bank.
n:Banco de Bogotá: Banco de Bogota is a bank in Bogota. Gerardo Hernandez Correa had served as a codirector of the Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, and also as its executive manager and the secretary of its Board. From 2021 he worked at Banco de Bogota as vice-president of legal affairs. He was later named president of Banco AV Villas, announced on 27 June 2024.
n:Banco de Poupança e Crédito (BPC): Banco de Poupanca e Credito, or BPC, is a state-owned bank in Luanda. Jose de Lima Massano was an executive director there, and chief executive of Banco BAI, before becoming Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, Angola's central bank, a job he held for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023. He left the central bank in June 2023 to become Senior Minister in the President's office.
n:Banka Kombëtare Tregtare: Banka Kombetare Tregtare is a bank in Tirana. Its link to the Bank of Albania is one man's career. Gent Sejko held senior executive posts and chaired committees at Banka Kombetare Tregtare and at other Albanian banks, and came from Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania to become Governor of the Bank of Albania and chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015.
n:Belize Electricity Limited: Belize Electricity Limited is a company in Belize. Kareem Michael joined the Central Bank of Belize as a monetary economist in 2000 and was Deputy Director of its Research Department from 2008. In 2014 he left to be a senior business analyst at Belize Electricity Limited, then returned to the central bank as Deputy Governor in November 2017, Acting Governor on 13 August 2021 and Governor on 1 December 2021.
n:Bolsa Electrónica de Valores del Urugu: The Bolsa Electronica de Valores del Uruguay, or BEVSA, is an electronic securities exchange in Montevideo. Diego Labat was President of the Banco Central del Uruguay, the country's central bank, from 2020 to 2024. The year after that term ended, BEVSA's board named him its General Manager, a decision taken on 20 August 2025.
n:CBZ Holdings Limited: CBZ Holdings Limited is a commercial banking group based in Harare. John Mangudya was its chief executive, and he left that job to run Zimbabwe's central bank, taking over as Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe from 1 May 2014. That step from the top of a commercial bank into the governorship is the tie between the two.
n:Demerara Bank Limited: Demerara Bank Limited is a bank in Georgetown, Guyana. Rajendra Rampersaud sat as a Director at the Bank of Guyana, the country's central bank, until 2018. After that he became a Director of Demerara Bank Limited, moving from the board of the central bank to the board of a commercial bank.
n:Directorate of Public Prosecutions of: The Directorate of Public Prosecutions, in Gaborone, brings criminal cases on behalf of the state in Botswana. Headed by Stephen Tiroyakgosi, it called in Moses Pelaelo, Governor of the Bank of Botswana, to hear his account of 100 billion pula that the state alleged had been looted from the central bank by former president Ian Khama and former intelligence chief Isaac Kgosi. Tiroyakgosi said Pelaelo told them no money is missing from the Bank of Botswana, and that the investigation was continuing; the allegations are unproven. In the same affair a woman arrested on 17 October 2019 had been implicated with Khama, Kgosi and others in allegedly stealing 100 billion pula from the Bank of Botswana. High Court Judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and of a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated and referred the investigator to police for prosecution for perjury.
n:Ecobank Transnational Incorporated: Ecobank Transnational Incorporated is a bank with its base in Lome, Togo. Sheila M'mbijjewe was a non-executive director of Ecobank, meaning a board member who does not work in the business day to day, as well as a director of Standard Chartered Bank and a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers. She left that set of roles to become Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya.
n:Ernst & Young Cyprus: Ernst & Young Cyprus is an accounting and audit firm in Cyprus. Constantin Schendra worked there as a senior auditor from 2013 to 2014, part of a career in auditing that also took in Ernst & Young Moldova and an executive director post at Baker Tilly Moldova. He then joined the National Bank of Moldova, heading its Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021 and becoming Deputy Governor on 4 November 2021.
n:Ernst & Young Moldova: Ernst & Young Moldova is an accounting and audit firm in Chisinau. Constantin Schendra was a senior auditor there from 2010 to 2015, and worked in auditing elsewhere afterwards. He then moved into the National Bank of Moldova, where he ran the Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021 before being made Deputy Governor and a member of the Executive Committee on 4 November 2021.
n:Farallon Capital Management LLC: Farallon Capital Management LLC is a company based in the United States. Greg Swart was its Managing Member and Chief Financial Officer from 2002 to 2019, and had spent about twelve years at Goldman Sachs before that. He then took a seat as a Director on the board of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, moving from private finance to the body that oversees it.
n:Financial Intelligence Agency of Botsw: The Financial Intelligence Agency is based in Gaborone. Botswana's Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime confirmed it was investigating unaccounted-for funds on government accounts held at the Bank of Botswana, after the Auditor General reported that 22 billion pula in receipts and payments remained unaccounted for. The Financial Intelligence Agency was reported to have opened its own investigation into the same accounts, which its Director General would neither confirm nor deny. The investigations are open and nothing is proven.
n:Golomt Bank: Golomt Bank is a commercial bank in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. It is linked to the Bank of Mongolia, the country's central bank, through a person who worked at both. Khosjargal Undraa spent thirteen years at Golomt Bank, then worked at MIG LLC and BPM Mongolia LLC, and later became a member of the Bank of Mongolia's Supervisory Board. That is a career move between a commercial bank and the central bank, not a finding against either.
n:Government of Chad: The Government of Chad sits in N'Djamena. It is linked to BEAC, the Bank of Central African States, which issues money for a group of countries in the region, through one person's career. Abbas Mahamat Tolli was Chad's Minister of Finance and Budget, and also president of the Development Bank of Central African States, before becoming Governor of the Bank of Central African States from 2017 to 2024. The record is a career move and carries no accusation.
n:Government of Côte d'Ivoire: The Government of Côte d'Ivoire sits in Abidjan. It shares one career with the BCEAO, the Central Bank of West African States, which issues money for several countries in the region. Tiemoko Meyliet Kone joined the BCEAO in 1975, was its National Director from 1991 to 1998 and its Governor from 2011 to 2022. Before returning he was Ivorian Minister of Construction, Urban Planning and Housing, and chief of staff to Prime Minister Guillaume Soro; after the BCEAO he became Vice-President of Côte d'Ivoire.
n:Government of Djibouti: The Government of Djibouti, in the capital Djibouti, fills the board of the Central Bank of Djibouti. Under the statutes set by law number 118/AN/11/6eme L of 22 January 2011, that board consists of the Governor plus six administrators appointed by decree, so every seat other than the Governor's is chosen by the executive. The bank's own 2024 annual report describes the board as its supreme organ and repeats that composition, citing the 2011 law. The arrangement has no end date.
n:Government of Malawi: The Government of Malawi sits in Lilongwe. It is linked to the Reserve Bank of Malawi, the country's central bank, by one person's career. MacDonald Mafuta Mwale was Secretary to the Treasury in the Malawian government before moving to the Reserve Bank, where he served as Deputy Governor and was then appointed Governor with immediate effect, as reported on 7 January 2025. That is a move between government service and the central bank.
n:Government of Rwanda: The Government of Rwanda, in Kigali, is linked to two central banks through careers. John Rwangombwa was Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, and earlier Secretary to the Treasury and first Accountant General, before serving as Governor of the National Bank of Rwanda from 2013 until February 2025. Dr Ibrahim L. Stevens did macroeconomic advisory work for Rwanda's finance ministry before becoming Deputy Governor of the Bank of Sierra Leone in July 2014; he had been its Director of Research from 2008 to 2010, and later its Governor.
n:Government of Saint Vincent and the Gr: The Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines sits in Kingstown. It is linked to the ECCB, the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, which issues money for a group of island states, by one person's career. Sir Cecil Jacobs was the government's Financial Secretary before becoming Governor of the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, a post he held from 1973 to 1989. The connection is a move from a government finance post into the central bank.
n:Government of Tanzania: The Government of Tanzania sits in Dodoma. It shares a career with the Bank of Tanzania, the country's central bank. Emmanuel Tutuba was Permanent Secretary to the Treasury in the Ministry of Finance, and earlier budget commissioner in the same ministry, before being appointed Governor of the Bank of Tanzania on 7 January, in an appointment reported on 9 January 2023. That is a move from the finance ministry into the central bank, with nothing alleged against him.
n:Government of the Macao Special Admini: The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region appoints the board of the Monetary Authority of Macao, which issues and manages the territory's money. Macao's Chief Executive, Sam Hou Fai, named Vong Sin Man, a worker of the Statistics and Census Service, to the Authority's board from 1 July to 31 December 2025. The order was made under article 50 of the Basic Law and the Authority's statute, approved by Decree-Law 14/96/M of 11 March 1996, under which the head of the executive appoints the board.
n:Government of the Union of the Comoros: The Government of the Union of the Comoros, in Moroni, shares control of the Central Bank of the Comoros with France. Under statutes signed in Paris on 22 April 2008 and still in force, the board has at most eight members, half designated by the French Government and half by the Comorian government. The Governor is named by the President of the Union, on the Finance Minister's proposal. New draft statutes approved on 28 June 2024 still awaited promulgation at year's end.
n:Halyk Bank: Halyk Bank is a commercial bank in Almaty, Kazakhstan. Its tie to the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the country's central bank, runs through Grigory Marchenko, who chaired the National Bank from October 1999 until 2004 and then became chairman at Halyk Bank. An article dated 30 January 2009 reported that he had been appointed to chair the central bank a second time.
n:Investrust Bank Plc: Investrust Bank Plc is a commercial bank in Lusaka, Zambia. It is linked to the Bank of Zambia, the country's central bank, through one person's career. Dr Richard K. E. Chembe held senior management positions at the Bank of Zambia and at the International Monetary Fund, the lender that governments turn to for emergency loans, before becoming Managing Director of Investrust Bank Plc with effect from 1 May 2015. Nothing is alleged against him.
n:Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC: Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC is a bank in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Its tie to Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank, is through Md. Khurshid Alam, who was appointed a Deputy Governor of Bangladesh Bank in February 2024 on a three-year contract and was forced to resign in August 2024. On 24 May 2026 he was appointed chairman of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC. The move between the two institutions is a career record, with no wrongdoing stated.
n:JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia: JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia is a commercial bank in Tbilisi, Georgia. It is linked to the National Bank of Georgia, the country's central bank, through Nino Jeladze. She worked at JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia and at ProCredit Holding in Frankfurt before joining the National Bank of Georgia, where she became head of the Supervisory Policy Department in 2024 and Vice-Governor and a member of the Board on 10 February 2025. That is a career move, not a complaint.
n:Joint Public Accounts Committee, Natio: The Joint Public Accounts Committee of Belize's National Assembly sits in Belmopan. Reporting on the Auditor General's report for April 2016 to March 2017, it prioritised significant material differences between Central Bank of Belize and SmartStream balances, of 42 million, 19 million, 3 million and 1.4 million dollars. At its March 2026 hearings Auditor General Maria Rodriguez said not even the Central Bank accounts were being reconciled. The 19,489,652.02 dollar difference for the Debt Service Escrow Account, the Committee recorded, was a typographical error, as the Auditor General confirmed.
n:Latin Securities: Latin Securities is a firm in Uruguay. Its tie to the Central Bank of Uruguay runs through Washington Ribeiro, who held three posts there: director from June 2010 to March 2020, vice president from March 2020 to July 2024, and president from July 2024 to March 2025. He then joined Latin Securities as head of Uruguayan macro and sovereign strategy. That is a move from the central bank into private finance, with nothing alleged.
n:Lithuanian parliamentary commission on: This was a commission of Lithuania's parliament, in Vilnius, set up to examine the collapse of the bank Snoras. Chaired by Valentinas Mazuronis, it found that the Bank of Lithuania, the country's central bank, acted too fast and with too little reasoning when it shut Snoras down in November 2011. Mazuronis said both the takeover of Snoras shares in the public interest and the start of bankruptcy proceedings were hasty and not sufficiently reasoned.
n:Mahmoud Abbas: Mahmoud Abbas is the President of Palestine, based in Ramallah, and he appoints the board of the Palestine Monetary Authority, which carries out central banking for Palestine. He issued a presidential decree reconstituting that board, acting on recommendations from the Cabinet and from the Authority's Governor. Three of the eight seats are held by virtue of law: the Governor, who chairs the board, the Deputy Governor, and a representative of the Ministry of Finance, named as Majdi Al-Hassan.
n:Maria Rodriguez: Maria Rodriguez is the Auditor General of Belize, based in Belmopan, the official who checks the government's accounts. At hearings of the National Assembly's Joint Public Accounts Committee in March 2026 she said that not even the Central Bank of Belize accounts were being reconciled, and pointed to differences between confirmation letters from the bank and the government's own records. She also confirmed that a 19,489,652.02 dollar difference recorded for the Debt Service Escrow Account was a typographical error, with no actual difference.
n:Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas de Gua: Guatemala's Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas, the finance ministry, is in Guatemala City. Alvaro Gonzalez Ricci was its Minister of Public Finance, a post he took up in January 2020, before becoming president of the Banco de Guatemala, the country's central bank. Emisoras Unidas reported on 1 October 2022 that he had taken the central bank post for a four-year term running to 20 September 2026. The move from ministry to central bank carries no allegation.
n:Ministry of Finance of Eswatini: The Ministry of Finance of Eswatini is in Mbabane. It shares a career with the Central Bank of Eswatini, the country's central bank. Martin Dlamini was Governor of the Central Bank from July 1997 to November 2013, and then became the country's Minister of Finance. That is a move from the central bank into the government department that manages public money, and nothing is alleged against him in connection with it.
n:Ministry of Finance of Moldova: The Ministry of Finance of Moldova is in Chisinau. It is linked to the National Bank of Moldova, the country's central bank, through Octavian Armasu. He was Moldova's Minister of Finance before being appointed Governor of the National Bank on 30 November 2018, for a seven-year term. The connection is a straightforward move from the finance ministry into the central bank, with no accusation attached to it.
n:Ministry of Finance of Montenegro: The Ministry of Finance of Montenegro is in Podgorica. It shares a career with the Central Bank of Montenegro. Radoje Zugic was the central bank's Deputy Director General for Payment System Operations from 2001 to 2004 and its Governor from 2010 to 2012, then served as Montenegro's Minister of Finance and afterwards as adviser to the Prime Minister. He returned as Governor of the central bank in October 2016. These are job changes, not findings against him.
n:Ministry of Finance of North Macedonia: The Ministry of Finance of North Macedonia is in Skopje. It is linked to the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia, the country's central bank, through Anita Angelovska Bezhoska. She managed the ministry's Treasury Department and was State Secretary there, and worked as an economist in the European Department of the International Monetary Fund, before becoming Vice-Governor and then Governor of the National Bank. That is a career path between ministry and central bank.
n:Ministry of Finance of Uzbekistan: The Ministry of Finance of Uzbekistan is in Tashkent. Timur Ishmetov has moved between it and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan more than once: he went from First Deputy Chairman of the Central Bank to First Deputy Minister of Finance, having earlier been First Deputy Chairman of the State Committee for Investments, and later served as Minister of Finance. He was then made Chairman of the Central Bank, with the appointment taking effect on 11 December 2024.
n:Ministry of Finance of Venezuela: The Ministry of Finance of Venezuela is the Venezuelan government's finance ministry, based in Caracas. Its link to the Central Bank of Venezuela is a shared official. Nelson Merentes, president of the central bank since 2009, moved from that post to become Minister of Finance in the government of Venezuela. That is the tie on record: one person holding the top job at the central bank and then the ministry.
n:Ministry of Finance of the Maldives: The Ministry of Finance of the Maldives is the Maldivian government's finance ministry, based in Malé. It is tied to the Maldives Monetary Authority, the country's central bank, through a shared official. Ali Hashim served as the government's finance minister and was then nominated, in August 2019, to be Governor of the Monetary Authority. At the time of reporting he was the nominee rather than the sitting governor.
n:Nepal Investment Board: The Nepal Investment Board is a state body in Kathmandu. It shares an official with Nepal Rastra Bank, the country's central bank. Maha Prasad Adhikari retired as deputy governor of the bank in December 2015, after three decades there, and became chief executive officer of the Investment Board. He then returned to the central bank as its seventeenth governor, appointed on 6 April 2020 for a five-year term.
n:New Zealand Superannuation Fund: The New Zealand Superannuation Fund is a state investment body based in Auckland. It shares an official with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, the country's central bank. Adrian Orr had moved from chief economist at the bank Westpac to Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank, and later came from the Superannuation Fund to become Governor of the Reserve Bank from 27 March 2018.
n:Office of the Auditor General of Beliz: The Office of the Auditor General of Belize, in Belmopan, audits government accounts. For the 2011/2012 financial year it reported that the Treasury could not show that 25 bank accounts held by the Central Bank of Belize for the Government of Belize had been reconciled for the period audited. It also found the Commonwealth Secretariat public debt recording system run by the central bank did not match the Accountant General's statements, and that interest payments recorded by the central bank differed from the government's Smart Stream records.
n:PASHA Bank: PASHA Bank is a commercial bank in Baku, Azerbaijan. It shares an official with the Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Taleh Kazimov rose at PASHA Bank from risk manager to chief executive officer and then chairman, before being made Governor of the central bank by a parliamentary vote reported on 18 April 2022. The move from the bank to the governorship is the tie here.
n:ProCredit Holding AG: ProCredit Holding AG is a company based in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. It shares an official with the National Bank of Georgia, Georgia's central bank. Nino Jeladze came from JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia and ProCredit Holding in Frankfurt to the National Bank of Georgia, where she became Head of the Supervisory Policy Department in 2024 and then Vice-Governor and a member of the Board on 10 February 2025.
n:Raiffeisen Bank Albania: Raiffeisen Bank Albania is a commercial bank in Tirana. It shares an official with the Bank of Albania, the country's central bank. Gent Sejko held senior executive and committee-chairing roles at the National Commercial Bank, the American Bank of Albania and Raiffeisen Bank, and came from being Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania to be Governor of the Bank of Albania and Chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015.
n:Raiffeisen Bank d.d. Bosna i Hercegovi: Raiffeisen Bank d.d. Bosna i Hercegovina is a commercial bank in Sarajevo. It shares an official with the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Jasmina Selimovic was an independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank BiH in 2018, and joined the central bank's Governing Board on 3 January 2024, later becoming Governor and chair of that board. She had also been president of the board of directors of the Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance since 2021.
Raiffeisenbank a.s. is a commercial bank in Prague, Czechia. It shares an official with the Czech National Bank. Aleš Michl worked at Raiffeisenbank as an economist and investment strategist, then joined the Czech National Bank's board in December 2018 and later became its governor. The move from the commercial bank into the central bank's board and then its top job is what connects the two.
n:Royal Government of Bhutan: The Royal Government of Bhutan, in Thimphu, appoints and can direct the board of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank. Under the Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan 2010, in force from 22 June 2010, section 149 lets the government issue such directives to the Authority as it considers necessary, after consulting the Governor and in the public interest, reporting them to Parliament. Four of the board's seven members are government appointees, one from the Ministry of Finance, and the government sets the Governor's salary.
n:Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health In: The Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance is a state body in Sarajevo, Bosnia. It shares an official with the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Jasmina Selimovic has been president of the Institute's board of directors since 2021, and went from there to the central bank's Governing Board, which she joined on 3 January 2024, later becoming Governor and chair of the board. She had earlier been an independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank BiH in 2018.
n:Senate of Rwanda: The Senate of Rwanda is one chamber of the country's parliament, in Kigali. It summoned Claver Gatete, governor of the National Bank of Rwanda, over the slide of the Rwandan franc, which had weakened 1.3 percent against the dollar in the first half of the year. Gatete appeared with finance minister John Rwangombwa and put the pressure down to speculation by investors who heard donors were cutting aid, saying the central bank had put 327.8 million US dollars into the foreign exchange market since 2011.
n:Societe Generale Albania: Societe Generale Albania is a commercial bank in Tirana. It shares an official with the Bank of Albania, the country's central bank. Gent Sejko moved from Deputy General Manager at Societe Generale Albania to Governor of the Bank of Albania and Chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015, and was re-elected for a second term on 24 February 2022. Before that he had held senior executive and committee-chairing roles at the National Commercial Bank, the American Bank of Albania and Raiffeisen Bank.
n:Stanbic Bank Zambia: Stanbic Bank Zambia is a commercial bank in Zambia; the map marker sits on the country rather than the exact office. It shares an official with the Bank of Zambia, the country's central bank. Dr Austin Mwape was Deputy Governor of Operations at the Bank of Zambia and then became chairman of the board of directors of Stanbic Bank Zambia from December 2016.
n:State Bank of Mongolia: The State Bank of Mongolia is a state-owned commercial bank in Ulaanbaatar. It shares an official with the Bank of Mongolia, the country's central bank. Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mongolia from 2007 to 2010 and its London representative, then worked at the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the AIIB, the International Investment Bank and the State Bank of Mongolia, before returning to the central bank's Supervisory Board as a member in 2025.
n:Stephen Tiroyakgosi: Stephen Tiroyakgosi heads Botswana's Directorate of Public Prosecutions, in Gaborone. In that role he called in Moses Pelaelo, governor of the Bank of Botswana, to hear his account of the 100 billion pula the state alleged had been taken from the central bank by former president Ian Khama and former intelligence chief Isaac Kgosi. Tiroyakgosi said Pelaelo told them no money was missing from the Bank of Botswana. The allegation is unproven and the investigation was continuing.
n:Stopanska Banka AD Skopje: Stopanska Banka AD Skopje is a commercial bank in Skopje, North Macedonia, and a member of the NBG Group. It shares an official with the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia.
