Dimitar Bogov was the bank's chief economist from 2002 to January 2007, then Vice Governor of the central bank from February 2007 to May 2011, and Governor from 2011.
n:Swedbank AB: Swedbank AB is a commercial bank in Stockholm, Sweden. It shares an official with Sveriges Riksbank, Sweden's central bank. Anna Breman was a senior economist at Swedbank from 2013 to 2015 and its group chief economist from 2015 to 2019, then became a Deputy Governor of the Riksbank from 2019 to 2022 and First Deputy Governor from 2022.
n:Teresita Miranda: Teresita Miranda, in Belmopan, is named in a documented matter involving the Central Bank of Belize. The Joint Public Accounts Committee of Belize's National Assembly, reporting on the Auditor General's report for April 2016 to March 2017, listed significant material differences between Central Bank and SmartStream balances as a priority area, with gaps of 42 million, 19 million, 3 million and 1.4 million dollars. It recorded that the 19,489,652.02 dollar gap for the Debt Service Escrow Account was a typing error, which the Auditor General confirmed.
n:Treasury Department, Government of Bel: The Treasury Department of the Government of Belize, in Belmopan, is named in an audit finding involving the Central Bank of Belize. For the 2011/2012 financial year the Auditor General of Belize reported that the Treasury could not show that 25 bank accounts held by the central bank on the government's behalf had been reconciled for the period audited. The same report found that interest payments recorded by the central bank differed from those in the government's Smart Stream system. No amounts were given for the findings.
n:United National Bank Limited: United National Bank Limited is a bank in London, United Kingdom. It shares an official with the State Bank of Pakistan, Pakistan's central bank. Yaseen Anwar worked at Bank of America from 1976 to 1991 and as a vice president at Merrill Lynch from 1992 to 2001, and was a non-executive director of United National Bank from 2000 to 2006. He was appointed Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan on 29 March 2007 and Governor on 19 October 2011.
n:Valentinas Mazuronis: Valentinas Mazuronis, in Vilnius, chaired a Lithuanian parliamentary commission that examined the Bank of Lithuania's closure of the bank Snoras in November 2011. The commission found the central bank had acted too fast and with too little reasoning. Mazuronis said the takeover of Snoras shares in the public interest and the opening of bankruptcy proceedings were both hasty and not sufficiently reasoned. This was the commission's own finding about the central bank's handling of the shutdown.
n:Westpac Banking Corporation: Westpac Banking Corporation is a bank based in Sydney, Australia. It shares an official with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, New Zealand's central bank. Adrian Orr was Westpac's chief economist before becoming Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank, and later came from the New Zealand Superannuation Fund to be Governor of the Reserve Bank from 27 March 2018.
n:Central Organization for Financial Con: The Central Organization for Financial Control is Syria's supreme audit institution, in Damascus. It audits the records and accounts of the Central Bank of Syria, within the limits of its own law, under article 68(3) of Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002. No private firm is appointed in its place, and no financial year is set: the mandate is a standing one written into the law governing the bank.
n:National Audit Authority: The National Audit Authority is Cambodia's supreme audit institution, in Phnom Penh. Under article 57-New of the law of 29 December 2006, the financial records of the National Bank of Cambodia are verified by the bank's own Board and by the Authority. The Authority is the outside half of that arrangement; the Board is an organ of the bank. No private firm is appointed and the law sets no financial year.
n:Accountant General of Barbados: The Accountant General of Barbados, in Bridgetown, keeps the government's books, and auditors have compared them with the Central Bank of Barbados. The 2004 Auditor General's report found that between October 2000 and February 2004 the two sets of records for the government current account did not match, with unrecorded withdrawals above $1.8 million and unrecorded deposits above $6.8 million, including a $4.48 million transaction flagged in 2003. The 2020 report found eight loan-fund transfers totalling $13.137 million made without the signed memorandum the Accountant General gives the bank.
n:Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba: Aruba's General Audit Chamber in Oranjestad checks how the country accounts for its money. Reviewing the annual accounts for 2001 to 2004, it found that money paid into an earmarked account held in Aruba's name at the Centrale Bank van Aruba for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation was not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Of a balance of 19.3 million Aruban florins at the end of 2000, only the 3 million paid in by Aruba appeared; 16,898,503 florins paid in by the Netherlands were left off.
n:Barbados Audit Office: The Barbados Audit Office in Bridgetown audits government accounts, several of which sit at the Central Bank of Barbados. Its 2004 report found records of the government current account not matching the bank's between October 2000 and February 2004. The 2020 report found Treasury accounts unreconciled since May 2018, eight loan-fund transfers totalling $13.137 million without the required memorandum, and the government overdraft twice passing its statutory limit of 10 per cent of estimated revenue, $323.303 million. The 2021 report found an unexplained $6,662,541.31 cheque difference for 22 September 2020.
n:Cabinet of Malta: Malta's Cabinet, the country's government ministers in Valletta, was reported to have settled how the governorship of the Central Bank of Malta would be handled while its governor faced criminal charges. Edward Scicluna stepped aside from his functions as governor, with deputy governor Alexander Demarco replacing him. Scicluna had insisted he would not resign, and a Tuesday cabinet meeting appeared to have reached a compromise with him. Prime Minister Robert Abela insisted on the presumption of innocence; the charges are unproven. Scicluna keeps his salary, put at 138,000 euros.
n:Cabinet of Solomon Islands: The Cabinet in Honiara is the government of the Solomon Islands and has a standing role at the Central Bank of Solomon Islands. Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, section 41(1) has the Governor-General appoint the Governor on Cabinet's recommendation and section 41(3) has the Minister for Finance appoint the other directors. Section 37 lets the Minister, with Cabinet's approval, give written directions, which must be published in the Gazette and laid before Parliament. Section 44 allows early removal only for permanent incapacity or serious misconduct.
n:Cabinet of Tonga: Tonga's Cabinet, the government in Nukuʻalofa, holds the appointments at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. Under the National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, section 10(1) has the Minister, with Cabinet's consent, appoint five directors and name the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, and section 11(1) has Cabinet appoint the Governor. Section 50(1) allows written directives, and under section 50(4) a policy disagreement goes to Cabinet to decide. Section 11(3) permits the Governor's removal only for incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties.
n:Cabinet of the Cayman Islands: The Cabinet of the Cayman Islands, the government in George Town, sits over the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority. Under the Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision), revised as at 31 December 2019 and still the main Act after a 2024 amendment touched only fees and regulation-making, section 12(1) has the Cabinet appoint the directors, section 11(3) designate the chairperson and deputy, and section 13(1) appoint the managing director. Section 33(1) lets it give written general directions in the public interest, which the Authority must follow.
n:Commission of inquiry of the Assembly: A commission of inquiry of the Comoros Assembly in Moroni examined the economic citizenship programme, which sold passports. Reporting in December 2017, it said that according to his own collaborators President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 the money no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores and could not explain what became of it; it concluded he was suspected of embezzling public money, which is unproven. It also found the programme account TR0044 took in money without the bank knowing what passports sold for.
n:Comoro Gulf Holding: Comoro Gulf Holding is a company in Moroni, Comoros, named in a parliamentary inquiry's account of money held at the Banque Centrale des Comores. The inquiry recorded that the economic citizenship account TR0044 at the central bank received payments including four cheques drawn by Comoro Gulf Holding on two commercial banks between March 2009 and April 2010, and that the bank booked money into the account without knowing the price at which the passports were being sold. The account was closed on 1 September 2015.
n:Council of Ministers of Syria: The Council of Ministers in Damascus is Syria's cabinet, and the law places the Central Bank of Syria under it. Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, says the Monetary and Credit Council, which sets monetary policy, works within the state's general economic directions as approved by the Council of Ministers. Under article 8(3) the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade may suspend a Council decision for up to seven days and refer a continuing disagreement to the Council of Ministers.
n:Câmara de Contas of Timor-Leste: The Câmara de Contas in Dili is Timor-Leste's Court of Accounts, which audits state accounts. In its report on the 2019 General State Account it found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union budget support, held in three accounts at the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, had not been booked as state revenue, so 2019 revenue was understated by that amount, and the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts went outside the state budget.
n:Government of Fiji: The Government of Fiji, based in Suva, removed the governor of the Reserve Bank of Fiji. Officials took Savenaca Narube out of the post and put deputy governor Sada Reddy in his place, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20 per cent. The government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason was given for the removal; Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3 per cent contraction for 2009.
n:Governor of Aruba: The Governor of Aruba, based in Oranjestad, holds the appointments at the Centrale Bank van Aruba. Under Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5, section 18 has the Governor appoint the president and executive directors from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and allows dismissal by state decree. Section 23 has the Governor appoint and dismiss the Government Commissioner, who chairs that board and supervises the bank on the Minister's instructions.
n:Ikililou Dhoinine: Ikililou Dhoinine, based in Moroni, is a former president of the Comoros. A Comorian parliamentary commission of inquiry into the economic citizenship programme, which sold Comorian nationality, reported in December 2017 that, according to his own collaborators, he ordered that from January 2015 until the end of his term the programme's money no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores, and that he could not explain what became of it. It concluded he was suspected of embezzling public money, which is unproven.
n:Legislative Assembly of El Salvador: The Legislative Assembly is El Salvador's parliament, in San Salvador. One of its commissions investigated the debt the government took on during the COVID-19 pandemic and how it was spent, and summoned Nicolás Martínez, president of the Banco Central de Reserva, the country's central bank. Deputies asked whether releasing the banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy government Treasury paper; he said that was an autonomous decision of the banks. He resigned the day after appearing, with no reason given.
n:Majlisi Namoyandagon of the Majlisi Ol: The Majlisi Namoyandagon is the lower house of Tajikistan's parliament, in Dushanbe, and its role over the National Bank of Tajikistan is approval only. The Law on the National Bank of Tajikistan, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, provides in article 74(4) that the Chairman and his deputies are appointed and released by presidential decree, with the decrees submitted to the lower house for approval. Article 74(3) has the board's three independent members approved by the President, and article 74(6) has him set their pay.
n:Ministry of Economy and Foreign Trade: This ministry, in Damascus, sits over the Central Bank of Syria. Under the Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, the bank's Monetary and Credit Council works within the state's general economic directions approved by the Council of Ministers. Article 8(3) lets the Minister suspend for up to seven days any Council decision he considers contrary to the state's interest, and refer a continuing disagreement to the Council of Ministers. Article 69 has the Governor appointed and removed by decree.
n:Ministry of Finance of Aruba: Aruba's finance ministry, in Oranjestad, shares control of the Centrale Bank van Aruba with the island's Governor. Under the Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5, section 18 has the president and executive directors appointed by the Governor from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board. Section 23 has the Governor appoint the supervisory directors, whose chairman is the Government Commissioner; under section 27(1) that Commissioner supervises the bank for the country and acts on the Minister's instructions.
n:Ministry of Finance of Bermuda: Bermuda's finance ministry, in Hamilton, appoints and can instruct the Bermuda Monetary Authority. Under the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969, section 21(2) lets the Minister give the Authority written general directions that appear to him necessary in the public interest, and the Authority must act in accordance with them. Section 4(1)(d) has eleven board members appointed by the Minister, section 4E(1) has him appoint the Chairman, and section 4E(6) lets him end the Chairman's appointment if satisfied he is unable or unfit. The arrangement is standing, with no end date.
n:Ministry of Finance of Solomon Islands: The finance ministry in Honiara draws its powers over the Central Bank of Solomon Islands from the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012. Section 37 lets the Minister, with Cabinet's approval, give the bank written directions on public-interest or policy-coordination grounds, but they must be published in the Gazette and laid before Parliament. Section 41(3) has the Minister appoint the other board directors after consulting the Governor. Section 44 allows removal before a term ends only for permanent incapacity or serious misconduct.
n:Ministry of Finance of Timor-Leste: Timor-Leste's finance ministry, in Dili, was named in findings by the country's Court of Accounts on the 2019 General State Account. The court found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union budget support, held in three accounts at the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, was not booked as state revenue, understating 2019 revenue by that amount, and that the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts was spent outside the state budget.
n:Ministry of Finance of Tonga: Tonga's finance ministry, in Nukuʻalofa, appoints most of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga's board. Under the National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, section 10(1) has the Minister, with Cabinet's consent, appoint five directors and the Chairman and Deputy Chairman. Section 11(3) allows the Governor's removal only for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Section 50(1) lets the Minister issue written directives with Cabinet's consent.
n:President of Tajikistan: The presidency, in Dushanbe, controls every seat on the board of the National Bank of Tajikistan, the country's central bank. Under the Law on the National Bank of Tajikistan, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, article 74(4) has the Chairman and his deputies appointed and released by presidential decree, with the decrees submitted to the lower house of parliament for approval. Article 74(3) has the board's three independent members approved by the President on the Chairman's proposal, and article 74(6) has him set their salaries.
n:Senate of Haiti: The Senate is the upper house of Haiti's parliament, in Port-au-Prince. Its Economy and Finance commission summoned Charles Castel, governor of the Banque de la République d'Haïti, the country's central bank, along with Ronald Baudin, Minister of Economy and Finance, to appear on Wednesday 1 June 2011. They were called to answer questions about new taxes of one dollar fifty US on each incoming or outgoing money transfer and five US cents a minute on incoming international calls.
n:Stichting Fondo Desaroyo Aruba: Stichting Fondo Desaroyo Aruba is a foundation based in Oranjestad. Aruba's General Audit Chamber, reviewing the country's annual accounts for 2001 to 2004, found that contributions paid for the foundation into an earmarked account held in the country's name at the Centrale Bank van Aruba were not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Of a balance of 19.3 million Aruban florins at the end of 2000, only the 3 million paid in by Aruba appeared in the accounts.
n:Government of Cabo Verde: The Government of Cabo Verde, in Praia, is given the job of setting monetary policy by the central bank's own founding law. The Organic Law of the Banco de Cabo Verde, Lei n.º 70/X/2026 of 26 January 2026, revokes the 2002 law and states that the Government defines monetary and exchange rate policy with the bank collaborating, while the bank carries that policy out on its own authority. Collaborating in that definition is listed among the duties of the bank's Board of Administration.
n:Council of Ministers of Cabo Verde: The Council of Ministers of Cabo Verde, in Praia, fills the leadership of the Banco de Cabo Verde. Under the Organic Law of 26 January 2026 it appoints the Governor and Vice-Governor on the proposal of the member of Government responsible for finance, appoints the non-executive members of the Supervisory Council the same way, and appoints the executive administrators on the Governor's proposal. Article 51 says they cannot be moved, and may be dismissed only for ceasing to meet the requirements of office or for serious misconduct, with a right of appeal.
n:Consiglio Grande e Generale of San Mar: The Consiglio Grande e Generale is San Marino's parliament. Under the Statute of the Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino, Law no. 96 of 29 June 2005 in the consolidated text in force from 30 November 2025, it appoints the bank's President and the five Councillors of the Governing Council, and the Director General appointed by that Council takes office subject to the parliament's approval. Every seat on the bank's governing bodies is filled this way.
n:Congress of State of San Marino: The Congress of State is San Marino's government. Under the central bank's Statute, Law no. 96 of 29 June 2005 in the text in force from 30 November 2025, it appoints two to four of its own members to the Committee for Credit and Savings, which is given the function of directing and orienting banking, financial and insurance supervision. The Statute does not say the Committee's directions bind the bank.
n:Secretary of State for Finance of San: The Secretary of State for Finance is San Marino's finance minister. Under article 48 of the central bank's Statute, Law no. 96 of 29 June 2005 in the text in force from 30 November 2025, he chairs the Committee for Credit and Savings, which is given the function of directing and orienting banking, financial and insurance supervision. The other members are appointed from the Congress of State. The Statute does not say the Committee's directions bind the bank.
n:Ministry of Finance of The Bahamas: The Bahamian finance ministry, in Nassau, stands behind every appointment to the Central Bank of The Bahamas and sets the policy the bank carries out. Under the Central Bank of The Bahamas Act 2020, the Governor, both Deputy Governors and six other directors are appointed, and a director or Deputy Governor removed, by the Governor-General on the Minister's advice after consulting the Board. Section 5(1)(f) makes the bank advise the Minister on exchange rate policy and implement the policy the Minister determines.
n:Governor-General of The Bahamas: The Governor-General is the Bahamian head of state's representative, in Nassau. Under the Central Bank of The Bahamas Act 2020 the formal power to appoint the bank's Governor, its two Deputy Governors and six other directors is the Governor-General's, and so is the power to remove a director or Deputy Governor. In each case the Act requires him to act on the advice of the Minister of Finance after consultation with the Board.
n:Papierfabrik Louisenthal: Louisenthal, also called Papierfabrik Louisenthal, is a firm in Gmund am Tegernsee, Germany, that makes the special paper banknotes are printed on. It says it supplied the security features embedded in the paper of the Bulgarian National Bank's 100-lev note — the thread, the foil and the watermark — though it names no particular paper product. That note became legal tender on 28 December 2018 and won the High Security Printing EMEA award in Malta in March 2019.
n:Byblos Bank Syria: Byblos Bank Syria is a commercial bank in Syria; no source opened gives the city of its head office, so its marker sits at the country rather than an exact address. Safwat Raslan, appointed Governor of the Central Bank of Syria in May 2026, had been a branch manager there, and before that worked in Germany as a banking expert at TARGOBANK and Deutsche Bank and as a credit business manager at a bank for doctors and pharmacists. The move is a career change and carries no accusation.
n:Ecofi Investissements: Ecofi Investissements is a French asset manager, a société de gestion within the Crédit Coopératif group; no source opened gives the city of its office, so its marker sits at the country. Karamo Kaba worked there as an economist strategist and then director of economic research from 2003 to 2021, before becoming the sixteenth Governor of the Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée in December 2021. Nothing is alleged against him.
n:MBANK: MBANK, formally OJSC Commercial Bank Kyrgyzstan, is a commercial bank in Kyrgyzstan; no source opened gives the city of its head office. Its audited accounts filed with the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange record a single private individual holding 97.97 per cent of its shares at the end of 2024, with no state body among the owners. Maksat Ishenbaev, a former deputy chairman of the board of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, became chairman of MBANK's board on 15 January 2025.
n:Sohar International Bank: Sohar International Bank is a commercial bank in Oman; no source opened gives the city of its head office. A published shareholding breakdown shows mixed ownership, with the state and government bodies holding about 12 per cent and the general public about 45 per cent. Ahmed Al Musalmi was its chief executive from 2018 until January 2025, when he was appointed Executive President of the Central Bank of Oman. The move is a career change and carries no accusation.
n:State Audit Bureau of Qatar: The State Audit Bureau is Qatar's state audit institution, in Doha. Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani headed it from 2015 to 2021 before becoming Governor of the Qatar Central Bank, having earlier spent part of his career inside the central bank itself. Because both sides of that career are public bodies, the map lists the move but does not count it among the moves through private finance.
n:Ministry of Finance of Nicaragua: Nicaragua's finance ministry, in Managua, employed Ovidio Reyes as its chief economist from 2004 to 2012, before he moved to the Banco Central de Nicaragua as general manager and then president. Both sides of that career are public bodies, so the map lists the move without counting it among the moves through private finance.
n:Department of Economic Affairs of Arub: Aruba's Department of Economic Affairs, in Oranjestad, is where Jeanette R. Semeleer worked as a management adviser, alongside the Department of External Relations, before joining the Centrale Bank van Aruba, which she went on to lead as President. Both sides of that career are public bodies, so the map lists the move without counting it among the moves through private finance.
n:Ministry of Economy and Industry of Ma: Mauritania's ministry of Economy and Industry, in Nouakchott, was headed from August 2019 by Mohamed El Cheikh El Kebir Moulaye, who had spent much of his earlier career inside the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, latterly as deputy governor, and who returned to the bank as its governor. Both sides of that career are public bodies, so the map lists the move without counting it.
n:Ministry of Finance and Economic Manag: Vanuatu's Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, in Port Vila, is where August Letlet served as Director General before being appointed Governor of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu. Both sides of that career are public bodies, so the map lists the move without counting it among the moves through private finance.
n:Ministry of Finance of São Tomé and Pr: The finance ministry of São Tomé and Príncipe, in São Tomé, was headed by Américo d'Oliveira dos Ramos as Minister of Finance between 2014 and 2018, before he became Governor of the Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe. Both sides of that career are public bodies, so the map lists the move without counting it among the moves through private finance.
n:Office of the Auditor-General (Kenya): The Office of the Auditor-General in Kenya audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Kenya, the country's central bank. Its report for the year ended 30 June 2025 was issued on 7 October 2025.
n:Office of the Auditor General (Zambia): The Auditor-General is Zambia's state audit office, and it audits the Bank of Zambia's accounts. Paragraph 15(2) of the First Schedule to the Bank of Zambia Act, No. 5 of 2022 says those accounts shall be audited annually, or whenever necessary, by the Auditor-General or by an auditor the Auditor-General appoints. So the arrangement is set by the law governing the bank rather than by a contract the bank awards, and no private firm is named in it.
n:Auditor General (South Sudan): The Auditor General is South Sudan's state audit office, and the law that created the central bank makes it the bank's auditor. Section 75(1) of the Bank of South Sudan Act 2011 names the Auditor General as the auditor of the bank's accounts and records, which it says shall be audited annually in accordance with International Standards on Auditing. The Act leaves room for a firm alongside it — section 76(1) refers to statements certified by the Auditor General and the bank's external auditors, and section 24(3)(h) has the Audit Committee recommend appointing an external audit firm — but the Act names no firm. A February 2023 notice from the Bank of South Sudan shows the Auditor General inviting private firms to bid for the external audit of the bank's statements for 2022 and 2023, without naming who won.
n:Auditor General (Guyana): The Auditor General is Guyana's state audit office, and it signed off on the Bank of Guyana's books. The bank's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2019 carry a Report of the External Auditors issued by the Auditor General, referenced AG: 30/2020 and dated 7 April 2020, and the Letter of Transmittal says the statements were certified by the external auditors appointed under section 60 of the Bank of Guyana Act. The report names the Auditor General as the auditor and names no private firm. The bank's registered office in those statements is in Georgetown.
n:Office of the Auditor General (Bermuda: The Office of the Auditor General is Bermuda's state audit office, and it audits the Bermuda Monetary Authority, which is the island's central bank and financial regulator. The Independent Auditor's Report in the Authority's 2021 annual report is addressed to the Board of Directors and issued by the Office of the Auditor General at Reid Hall, 3 Reid Street, Hamilton, signed by Heather Thomas, Auditor General, at Hamilton on 27 April 2022. No private firm is named as signing the opinion.
n:Contraloria General de la Republica (C: The Contraloria General de la Republica is Costa Rica's state audit body, in San Jose, and it is the outside check on the Banco Central de Costa Rica. Article 13 of the bank's own law, Ley Organica del Banco Central de Costa Rica, Ley No. 7558 of 1995, places the bank under the Contraloria's supervision, while articles 14 and 38 have the bank's own internal auditor countersign its balance sheets and financial statements. The law names no external audit firm, and it is still in force.
n:Contraloria General de la Republica (B: The Contraloria General de la Republica is Bolivia's state audit body, in La Paz, and the central bank's own law gives it the outside check on the Banco Central de Bolivia. Article 79 of Ley No. 1670, the Ley del Banco Central de Bolivia of 1995, assigns external governmental control of the bank to the commissions of the legislative chambers and to the Contraloria, and article 42 requires the bank to send its annual report and financial statements to the Contraloria within the first 120 days of each year. The law names no audit firm, and it is still in force.
n:AYA Bank: AYA Bank is a bank based in Yangon, Myanmar, and it is tied here to one central bank. Khin Saw Oo, formerly Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar, went from that post to Vice-Chairman of AYA Bank, joining the bank in 2018, and was re-designated Executive Chairman in May 2021. The bank's own leadership page sets out the appointment and the dates.
n:Banco Agrícola: Banco Agrícola is a bank based in San Salvador, El Salvador. Its tie to the Central Reserve Bank of El Salvador runs through one person. Rafael Barraza Domínguez served as President of the Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador, and earlier as its Vice-President and as its Studies and Economic Policy Manager, and then became Chief Executive Officer of Banco Agrícola.
n:Banco Ficohsa: Banco Ficohsa is a bank based in Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Wilfredo Rafael Cerrato Rodríguez, who became President of the Banco Central de Honduras on 27 January 2018, had earlier worked at Banco FICOHSA as a credit officer and then as an agency manager, from January 1997 to February 2003. That commercial banking spell, years before the central bank appointment, is the connection recorded here.
n:Banco Mercantil (Honduras): Banco Mercantil, S.A. is a bank based in Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Wilfredo Rafael Cerrato Rodríguez, who became President of the Banco Central de Honduras on 27 January 2018, worked at Banco Mercantil as a credit officer from November 1993 to April 1996. That was the first of several commercial banking jobs he held before the central bank appointment, more than twenty years later.
n:Banco Sicredi: Banco Sicredi is a bank based in Porto Alegre, Brazil, and the tie recorded here is to the Central Bank of Aruba. Thomas Domhoff, President of the Centrale Bank van Aruba from 1 July 2026, had held a directorship at Banco Sicredi, alongside project roles at ING, ABN AMRO, Rabobank and Capgemini, before taking up the central bank post.
n:Banco de la Producción (Banpro): Banco de la Producción, or Banpro, is a bank in Managua, Nicaragua. Luis Rivas Anduray was an economic adviser at the Banco Central de Nicaragua from 2001 to 2002, then ran the finance ministry's fiscal affairs office to 2003, and became Banpro's general manager at the end of 2004; he is now its chief executive. A report on the Nueva Tenedora Banpro holding states that Banpro's majority shareholder is Grupo Promerica, the second Central American financial group of private capital, and that Banpro was owned by Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga.
n:Bancolombia: Bancolombia is a bank based in Medellín, Colombia. Its corporate governance page states that Rafael Barraza Domínguez held the presidency, vice-presidency and studies and economic policy management of El Salvador's central bank, and is currently chief executive of Banco Agrícola. A rating report filed with the Salvadoran stock exchange states that Banco Agrícola's ultimate shareholder is Bancolombia, that the bank belongs to the Banagricola conglomerate owned by Bancolombia Panama, and that the three companies sit under the holding company Inversiones Financieras Banco Agricola, S.A.
n:Bank of Sahel and Sahara Community: The Bank of Sahel and Sahara Community is based in Tripoli, Libya, and the tie recorded here is to the Central Bank of Sudan. Mohamed Khair Ahmed Al-Zubair was its Vice President from 2002 to 2009 and became Governor of the Central Bank of Sudan in March 2011. Earlier he had been Sudan's Minister of Finance and National Economy from 2000 to 2001 and president of the board of the Saudi Sudanese Bank.
n:Deloitte (Malawi) with Deloitte & Touc: Deloitte (Malawi) with Deloitte & Touche (South Africa) is one joint appointment, naming the two Deloitte member firms that together hold the external audit of the Reserve Bank of Malawi, Malawi's central bank; the Malawian firm is in Blantyre. The joint auditors audited the central bank's consolidated and separate accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025, and the reports were signed on 30 June 2026.
n:Financial and Administrative Control B: The Financial and Administrative Control Bureau is Palestine's state audit body, which checks how public money is handled. In its 2020 annual report it qualified its audit of the Ministry of Finance's consolidated closing account, meaning it did not give those accounts a clean opinion. One finding was that the ministry had not disclosed an amount of 2,130,918 dinars that it owed to the Palestine Monetary Authority. The finding is against the ministry's disclosure; the Monetary Authority is the creditor.
n:First Bank of Nigeria: First Bank of Nigeria is a bank based in Lagos, Nigeria, and the tie here runs through its Gambian subsidiary. Alassan Jabby, also written Jabbie, joined the Central Bank of The Gambia in late 2004 as the accountant in charge of its treasury unit, and is now Executive Director and Business Development Manager of FirstBank Gambia Limited. FirstBank Gambia's own page states that it is a subsidiary of FirstBank of Nigeria Limited, which is listed on the Nigeria Stock Exchange with over 1.3 million shareholders.
n:FirstBank Gambia Limited: FirstBank Gambia Limited is a bank based in Banjul, Gambia. Its tie to the Central Bank of The Gambia runs through one person. Alassan Jabby, also written Jabbie, was the accountant in charge of the treasury unit at the Central Bank of The Gambia, which he joined in late 2004, and he went on to become Executive Director and Business Development Manager of FirstBank Gambia Limited.
n:Government of Uruguay: Uruguay's executive has standing constitutional powers over the Banco Central del Uruguay, an ente autonomo, or autonomous state body. Article 197 lets it object to and suspend such a body's acts and, if the objections are disregarded, order rectifications, correctives or removals. Article 198 lets it remove board members with the Senate's consent for ineptitude, omission or crime in office, or alone if the Senate does not rule within sixty days; such removals carry no right of appeal. Article 14 of the bank's charter designates its directors under article 187.
n:Grupo Promerica: Grupo Promerica is based in Panama City, Panama. Its tie to the Central Bank of Nicaragua runs through Luis Rivas Anduray, an economic adviser at the Banco Central de Nicaragua from 2001 to 2002, who later ran the finance ministry's fiscal affairs office to 2003 and became general manager of Banpro at the end of 2004, where he is now chief executive. A report on the Nueva Tenedora Banpro holding states that Grupo Promerica is Banpro's majority shareholder and the second Central American financial group of private capital.
n:Intermediaria Financiera, S.A. (Grupo: Intermediaria Financiera, S.A. is a company in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, and part of Grupo FICOHSA. Wilfredo Rafael Cerrato Rodríguez, who became President of the Banco Central de Honduras on 27 January 2018, worked there as a credit officer from September to December 1996. It was one of several commercial banking jobs he held in the 1990s and early 2000s, long before the central bank appointment.
n:Ivory Bank: Ivory Bank is a bank based in Juba, South Sudan. Addis Ababa Othow joined the Central Bank of Sudan as a banking inspector in 1997 and joined Ivory Bank in 1998. He joined the Bank of South Sudan in 2010 as head of its non-banking division, later worked for Equity Bank in Nairobi and in South Sudan, served as First Deputy Governor from 2022 to October 2023 and again from February 2025, and was appointed Governor in June 2025.
n:Kanbawza Bank (KBZ): Kanbawza Bank, known as KBZ, is a bank based in Yangon, Myanmar. Than Lwin was an economist at the Central Bank of Myanmar from 1966, became a Director in 1997, and served as Deputy Governor and Controller of Foreign Exchange from 1997 to 2003. In 2004 he joined Kanbawza Bank as a consultant, and he is listed as its Deputy Chairman. An interview with KBZ's senior managing director calls it Myanmar's largest privately owned financial institution and the largest of the country's 19 privately owned banks.
n:Karafarin Bank: Karafarin Bank is a privately owned bank based in Tehran, Iran. Its tie to the Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran runs through one appointment. Valiollah Seif was managing director of Karafarin Bank before he was appointed Governor of the Central Bank of Iran in August 2013.
n:Ministry of Finance of Palestine: The Ministry of Finance of Palestine appears here through an audit of its own accounts. In its 2020 annual report, Palestine's Financial and Administrative Control Bureau qualified its audit of the ministry's consolidated closing account, meaning it did not give those accounts a clean opinion. One finding was that the ministry had not disclosed an amount of 2,130,918 dinars that it owed to the Palestine Monetary Authority. The finding is against the ministry's disclosure; the Monetary Authority is the creditor.
n:National Pension & Provident Fund of B: The National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan, based in Thimphu, is the country's pension and provident fund. Dasho Penjore was Deputy Managing Director of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank, from 2003 to 2006, then served as Chief Chamberlain to the King and as Chief Executive Officer of the National Pension & Provident Fund, and became Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority in December 2015.
n:Palestine Islamic Bank: Palestine Islamic Bank is a bank in Palestine, and its tie to the Palestine Monetary Authority runs through one appointment. Yahya Shunnar was a director at the Palestine Islamic Bank and vice-chairman of Tamkeen Insurance Company, and he took office as Governor of the Palestine Monetary Authority on 4 January 2025.
n:President of Guyana: The President of Guyana holds powers over the Bank of Guyana under the Bank of Guyana Act, Chapter 85:02, Act No. 19 of 1998, enacted 31 December 1998. Section 3(1) describes the Bank as an autonomous institution governed by that Act. Section 14(2) lets the President end the Governor's appointment, and the Minister end any other Director's, on stated grounds. Under section 29 the Minister, in consultation with the Bank, sets the policies, principles and criteria of Guyana's exchange rate system, and the Bank handles only its day-to-day administration.
n:Rawbank: Rawbank is a bank based in Kinshasa, DR Congo. Its tie to the Central Bank of the Congo runs through one person. Leny Ilondo was a Director at the Central Bank of Congo until his retirement, and has sat on Rawbank's board as a non-executive director since 2024, serving on its risk and audit committees.
n:Richard Gibson: Richard Gibson was Curaçao's finance minister. A report of 26 May 2017 said the Supervisory Board of the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten had voted three to two to extend a managing director's term, short of the supermajority required, and that Gibson had written to the board members Robert Pietersz, Tom Kok, Miriela Carolina, Vance Williams and Hubert Lopez asking them to work on a solution. He said that without a solution there would be no other choice but dismissal of the board.
n:Saudi Sudanese Bank: The Saudi Sudanese Bank is based in Khartoum, Sudan. Mohamed Khair Ahmed Al-Zubair was president of its board, and was Sudan's Minister of Finance and National Economy from 2000 to 2001 and Vice President of the Bank of Sahel and Sahara Community from 2002 to 2009, before becoming Governor of the Central Bank of Sudan in March 2011.
n:Standard Lesotho Bank Limited: Standard Lesotho Bank Limited is a bank based in Maseru, Lesotho. Mr. O. 'Nete worked at Standard Bank of Lesotho as Senior Finance Manager, Finance Manager and Senior Manager Personal Credit, and earlier as Tax Manager at Stanlib, and now sits as a Non-Executive Director on the board of the Central Bank of Lesotho.
n:Stanlib: Stanlib is a company based in Maseru, Lesotho. Mr. O. 'Nete was its Tax Manager, and later held the posts of Senior Finance Manager, Finance Manager and Senior Manager Personal Credit at Standard Bank of Lesotho, before becoming a Non-Executive Director on the board of the Central Bank of Lesotho.
n:Tamkeen Insurance Company: Tamkeen Insurance Company is an insurance company based in Palestine, and it appears here through one career move. Yahya Shunnar was vice-chairman of Tamkeen Insurance Company and a director at the Palestine Islamic Bank, and he took office as Governor of the Palestine Monetary Authority on 4 January 2025.
n:Trade Bank of Iraq: The Trade Bank of Iraq is a bank based in Baghdad, Iraq, and the tie recorded here is a single career move. Faisal Wisam al-Heims was Director-General of the Trade Bank of Iraq before he was appointed Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq in March 2023.
n:Acadian Asset Management: Acadian Asset Management is an investment management firm based in Boston, in the United States. The tie to a central bank is a shared person. Ajmal Ahmady worked as a sovereign analyst at Acadian from 2009 to 2012, between jobs at T. Rowe Price from 2008 to 2009 and Fortress Investment Group from 2012 to 2014, and later became Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:BNP Paribas El Djazaïr: BNP Paribas El Djazaïr is a bank in Algiers, Algeria. Its link to a central bank is one person's career. Mohamed Lamine Lebbou worked at BNP Paribas El Djazaïr from 2004 to 2006. He then headed the state-owned Banque nationale d'Algérie from 2021 to 2024 and BEA International Bank from May 2025, and was appointed Governor of the Banque d'Algérie, the Bank of Algeria, in February 2026.
n:Banco de Reservas: Banco de Reservas is a bank in Santo Domingo, in the Dominican Republic. One central bank is tied to it through a shared person. George Manuel Hazoury was an administrator of Banco de Reservas before becoming a member of the Junta Monetaria, the monetary board of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana. He sat on that board until he was replaced under decree 532-20 in 2020.
n:Banco di Caribe: Banco di Caribe is a bank in Willemstad, Curaçao. One central bank is tied to it through a shared person. José Jardim was Financial Economic Director and a member of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten from 2017 until 30 June 2025. He then became Chief Executive Officer of Banco di Caribe, effective 1 July 2025.
n:Bank of Bhutan: Bank of Bhutan is a bank in Thimphu, Bhutan. Damche Tenzin worked at Bank of Bhutan Limited as Chief Legal Advisor and Company Secretary, then as Chief Support Officer, from September 2008 to December 2014. He went on to be Chief General Counsel of the National Pension & Provident Fund, and from 1 June 2016 Chief General Counsel of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank.
n:Branislav Gulev: Branislav Gulev is in Skopje, North Macedonia. He took part in the State Audit Office's audit of the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 financial statements. The final report of 4 March 2005 found improper and unlawful use of funds: the bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and in January 2004 foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from its guarantee deposit. It also found purchases of 30,210 thousand denars made without following the Public Procurement Law.
n:Fortress Investment Group: Fortress Investment Group is an investment firm based in New York, in the United States. The tie to a central bank is a shared person. Ajmal Ahmady worked in emerging market trading at Fortress from 2012 to 2014, after a fixed income job at T. Rowe Price from 2008 to 2009 and sovereign analysis at Acadian Asset Management from 2009 to 2012. He was Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:Government of Samoa: The Government of Samoa, in Apia, pressed ahead with changes to the Central Bank of Samoa's law widening the Finance Minister's role and moving some of the bank's rules into regulations. In a letter to the Attorney-General's office the bank said the changes could weaken its independence, increase political influence and create legal uncertainty. The International Monetary Fund wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 with the same warning about the bank's autonomy; Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt rejected the warnings as outside interference.
n:Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao S: Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt is the Prime Minister of Samoa, in Apia. His government pressed ahead with changes to the Central Bank of Samoa's law that would widen the Finance Minister's role and move some of the bank's rules into regulations. The International Monetary Fund wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 warning the reforms could weaken the bank's autonomy, and Schmidt rejected those warnings as outside interference. The central bank itself had told the Attorney-General's office the changes could weaken its independence.
n:Liberty Life Lesotho: Liberty Life Lesotho is a company based in Maseru, Lesotho. Its tie to a central bank is a shared person. Mrs M. Mohasoa was a member of its board and chairman of its audit and risk committee from 2017 to 2021, and later became a non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho, which issues the country's money.
n:Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah is the President of Namibia, in Windhoek. In the question-and-answer session after her State of the Nation Address she said the reported losses at the Bank of Namibia, Namibia's central bank, together with missing Government Institutions Pension Fund money, were smelling of corruption and must be investigated. Job Amupanda, leader of Affirmative Repositioning, said the central bank had made a loss close to a billion dollars for unexplained reasons. These are remarks, not findings, and no investigation is reported as ordered.
n:Samoa Audit Office: The Samoa Audit Office is based in Apia, Samoa. Its 2014 performance audit of government debt servicing compared when repayments were due with the dates the Central Bank of Samoa actually made them, and found instances where repayments had been delayed. It also recorded that there was no formalised arrangement between the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank. Its recommendations went to the Ministry of Finance, including that the two bodies formalise their responsibilities. No wrongdoing by any person is alleged.
n:Spitamen Bank: Spitamen Bank is a bank in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Four officials of the National Bank of Tajikistan, the country's central bank, have moved to its boards. Navruz Samandarzoda, who headed the central bank's research and modelling department, joined in January 2018 and later became Chairman of its Management Board. Sanovbar Dzhabirova, deputy director of the central bank's accounting department, and Mahmud Hamralizoda, deputy head of its international relations department, joined the Supervisory Board in January 2023, and Dilbar Khuseynova, head of insurance control from 2017 to 2024, in October 2024.
n:Standard Bank Group: Standard Bank Group is a stock-exchange-listed private banking group in Johannesburg, South Africa. Mrs M. Mohasoa, a non-executive director of the Central Bank of Lesotho, was a member of the board and chairman of the audit and risk committee of the insurer Liberty Life Lesotho from 2017 to 2021. Ownership is documented: the South African Reserve Bank's list of designated entities names Liberty Life Lesotho Ltd within the Liberty Insurance Group, and Liberty Holdings' 2019 annual report states Standard Bank Group Limited holds 53.6% of Liberty's issued ordinary share capital.
n:State Audit Office of the Republic of: The State Audit Office of the Republic of Macedonia, based in Skopje, audited the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 accounts from 12 October to 20 December 2004. Its final report of 4 March 2005 found improper and unlawful use of funds: the bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and in January 2004 foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from its guarantee deposit. It also found 30,210 thousand denars of purchases, 35.61 percent of those audited, made without following the Public Procurement Law.
n:T. Rowe Price: T. Rowe Price is an investment management firm based in Baltimore, in the United States. Ajmal Ahmady was a fixed income analyst there from 2008 to 2009. He then worked as a sovereign analyst at Acadian Asset Management from 2009 to 2012 and in emerging market trading at Fortress Investment Group from 2012 to 2014, and was Acting Governor of Da Afghanistan Bank, the Afghan central bank, from 3 June 2020 to 15 August 2021.
n:United Group Holdings: United Group Holdings is a privately held group in Willemstad, Curaçao, headed by Curaçao businessman Gregory Elias. It has wholly owned the commercial bank Banco di Caribe since 2022. José Jardim, a board member of the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten since 2017 responsible for financial and economic supervision and monetary policy, became chief executive of Banco di Caribe effective 1 July, ending an eight-year tenure at the central bank. The central bank announced his departure effective 30 June 2025 without naming his new employer.
n:A&P Investment Fund Management: A&P Investment Fund Management is an asset manager in Macao, meaning a firm that invests money on behalf of clients. Antonio Jose Felix Pontes was Executive Director of the Monetary Authority of Macao, the body that acts as Macao's central bank, and was also Macao Insurance Commissioner and a member of the authority's Advisory Council. He went on to become a board director and Chief Compliance Officer of A&P Investment Fund Management, and a non-executive director of Well Link Bank, Ltd.
n:Alpha Capital Partners: Alpha Capital Partners is an asset manager in Kampala, Uganda, meaning a firm that invests money on behalf of clients. Stephen Mpuuga Kaboyo held senior executive positions at the Bank of Uganda, the country's central bank, and then founded Alpha Capital Partners, where he is Managing Director.
n:Banco Popular de Ahorro: Banco Popular de Ahorro is a bank in Havana, Cuba. Joaquin Alonso Vazquez spent seven years as its vice president, up to 2017, and then served as president of CADECA S.A. From February 2023 he has been Minister President of the Banco Central de Cuba, the island's central bank, which sets Cuba's money policy and issues its currency.
n:Banco Unión S.A. (Bolivia): Banco Union S.A. is a bank in La Paz, Bolivia. Jaime Valencia Valencia worked at the bank, and he has twice been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, which issues the country's money: from 1996 to 2006, and again from 16 January 2020.
Banco de Cochabamba S.A. is a bank in the city of Cochabamba, Bolivia. It appears among the financial employers listed on the published career history of Jaime Valencia Valencia, who has been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, from 1996 to 2006 and again from 16 January 2020. The 1999 annual report of ASFI, Bolivia's financial regulator, lists Banco de Cochabamba S.A. among entities in liquidation, that is, being wound up.
n:Banque Centrale des Comores strongroom: This is the Banque Centrale des Comores' own strongroom, a secure vault inside the bank, in the capital Moroni. It is where the central bank of the Comoros keeps the gold it owns. The bank's audited accounts for the year ending 31 December 2024 record, in note 5 on gold holdings, eighteen bars held in that strongroom.
n:Belarusbank: Belarusbank is a bank in Minsk, Belarus. Nadezhda Yermakova chaired its board, then chaired the National Bank of Belarus, the country's central bank, from 2011 to 2014. She ran the interim administration of another Minsk bank, Belgazprombank, from 15 June to 11 December 2020, and on 15 January 2021 was appointed head of its board of directors. Belgazprombank's shares are held by Russia's Gazprom PJSC and Gazprombank JSC, 49.66 per cent each, Gazprom Transgaz Belarus with 0.49 per cent and the Belarusian state, through its Ministry of Energy, with 0.097 per cent.
n:Belgazprombank: Belgazprombank is a bank in Minsk, Belarus, and almost all of it belongs to the Gazprom group. Its shares are held by Russia's Gazprom PJSC and Gazprombank JSC at 49.66 per cent each, Gazprom Transgaz Belarus at 0.49 per cent and the Belarusian state, through its Ministry of Energy, at 0.097 per cent. Nadezhda Yermakova chaired the National Bank of Belarus, the country's central bank, from 2011 to 2014. On 15 January 2021 she was appointed head of the board of directors of Belgazprombank OJSC.
CADECA S.A., in Havana, is Cuba's state currency-exchange entity. Joaquin Alonso Vazquez was its president, after seven years as vice president of the bank Banco Popular de Ahorro up to 2017. From February 2023 he has been Minister President of the Banco Central de Cuba, the island's central bank, which issues Cuba's currency and sets its money policy.
n:Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (: The Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie, or CNAM, is a state agency in Nouakchott that runs health insurance in Mauritania. Abdel Aziz Ould Dahi was its Director General, and in January 2015 he became Governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, the country's central bank, which issues its money.
n:Central Bank of Iraq vault, Baghdad: This is the Central Bank of Iraq's own vault in Baghdad, where the bank keeps gold it owns. In note 4 of its financial statements for the year ending 31 December 2025, the bank separates its gold into three lines: gold held abroad, gold held in its own vault, and gold coins held in its own vault. The holding kept abroad is much the largest of the three, and is not placed with any named institution.
n:Central Bank of the Russian Federation: These are the Bank of Russia's own vaults, where Russia's central bank keeps the gold it owns. The holding comes to 2,283 tonnes, the sixth largest on this map. The bank's Annual Report 2025 states only that the assets are stored in Russia, without naming where. The bank has itself said, in remarks carried by the news agency Interfax, that it has taken no gold out of the country and that all of it sits in its own storage facilities on Russian territory.
Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. is an insurer in La Paz, Bolivia. It appears among the financial employers listed on the published career history of Jaime Valencia Valencia, who has twice been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, which issues the country's money: from 1996 to 2006, and again from 16 January 2020.
n:El Nilein Bank: El Nilein Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was General Manager of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1964 to 1967. He then ran El Nilein Bank as its General Manager from 1970 to 1973, and went back to the central bank as Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors from 1973 to 1980.
n:Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Industry: This is a government ministry in Port Vila, Vanuatu, covering trade, commerce, industry and tourism. Marakon Alilee was its Director General, and had held senior posts earlier at the Vanuatu Chamber of Commerce, Airports Vanuatu Limited, VANAIR and the Vanuatu National Provident Fund. On 12 September 2014 he was appointed to the board of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, the country's central bank.
n:National Bank (Sudan): National Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1973 to 1980. He left to become General Manager of National Bank from 1980 to 1982, and later General Manager of Workers National Bank from 1989 to 1992.
n:Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage: Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage is a brokerage in Seoul, South Korea, meaning a firm that arranges currency trades between other institutions. Jeong Gyu-il joined the Bank of Korea, the country's central bank, in 1987 and rose to Deputy Governor. His appointment as chief executive and president of Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage was announced on 2 July 2021.
n:Well Link Bank: Well Link Bank is a bank in Macao, and its own history page describes it as a fully licensed commercial bank registered in Macao. That is what makes the career below a move into private banking rather than between state bodies. Antonio Jose Felix Pontes was Executive Director of the Monetary Authority of Macao, the body that acts as Macao's central bank, and was also Macao Insurance Commissioner and a member of the authority's Advisory Council. He went on to become a Non-Executive Director of Well Link Bank, Ltd., and a board director and Chief Compliance Officer of the asset manager A&P Investment Fund Management.
n:Workers National Bank (Sudan): Workers National Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1973 to 1980. He then served as General Manager of National Bank from 1980 to 1982, and as General Manager of Workers National Bank from 1989 to 1992.
n:BDO & Co, Chartered Accountants (Mauri: BDO & Co, Chartered Accountants is an accountancy firm in Port Louis, Mauritius. It is the external auditor of the Bank of Mauritius, the central bank of Mauritius, which means it is the outside firm brought in to check the bank's accounts and say whether they give a true picture. It audited the accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025.
n:BDO Chartered Accountants (Samoa): BDO Chartered Accountants is an accounting firm in Apia, Samoa. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Samoa, signing off that bank's financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2025, so the figures the central bank publishes for that year carry this firm's name.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers Limited (Cyprus: PricewaterhouseCoopers Limited is a private accounting firm in Nicosia, Cyprus. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Cyprus, and its approved term covered the financial years 2018 to 2022. Auditors of national central banks in the European Union are approved by a formal decision of the Council of the EU, Council Decision 1999/70/EC, the consolidated version of which dates from 26 October 2021. That is the one central bank it is tied to here.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL (Barbados): PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL is the Barbadian practice of the accounting and auditing firm PricewaterhouseCoopers, at The Financial Services Centre, Bishop's Court Hill. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Barbados, which means it examines the bank's financial statements and signs a report saying whether they give a fair picture of its finances. Its report sits at pages 61 to 64 of the bank's Annual Report 2025 and is dated at Bridgetown on 27 March 2026, for the year ended 31 December 2025. The report says it is made to the board of directors under section 67 of the Central Bank of Barbados Act, 2020.
n:Oberthur Fiduciaire AD (Bulgaria): Oberthur Fiduciaire AD prints the banknotes of the Bulgarian National Bank, the one central bank it is tied to. Louisenthal states that Oberthur Fiduciaire AD has handled Bulgarian National Bank banknote production since 2014. Nothing else is reported about it.
n:Arab Italian Bank (UBAE): Arab Italian Bank (UBAE) is a bank, and one person links it to the Central Bank of Libya. Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf joined the Central Bank of Libya in 1985 and was Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012, and again from 2024. Between 2005 and 2012 he also sat on the board of Arab Italian Bank (UBAE).
n:Barings LLC: Barings LLC is a firm that invests money for clients. Timor-Leste's central bank, the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, is the operational manager of the country's Petroleum Fund and hires outside firms to run parts of it. Its quarterly report for 30 June 2025 lists Barings as the manager of the Barings LLC 1-10 years US TIPS mandate, and says the outside managers' investments stayed within their mandates during the quarter.
n:Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corrupti: The Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption and Funds Recovery Committee, in Khartoum, was set up by Sudan's transitional government. Radio Dabanga reported on 9 February 2020 that the committee dissolved the board of directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, along with the boards of eleven other banks, and that nine of the central bank's managers were dismissed at the same time. The reason given was the bank's alleged links to the deposed government of Omar Al Bashir, an allegation that remains unproven. No individual board member was named.
n:Franklin Templeton: Franklin Templeton invests money on behalf of clients. The Banco Central de Timor-Leste runs the country's Petroleum Fund day to day and hands parts of it to outside firms. The bank's quarterly report for 30 June 2025 lists Franklin Templeton as the manager of the Franklin Templeton 1-10 years US TIPS mandate, and records that the outside managers' investments stayed within their mandates over the quarter.
Goldman Sachs Asset Management L.P. invests money on behalf of clients and is tied to two central banks. Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, names it in its reserves management report as one of the seven outside firms each running a dedicated actively managed portfolio of Colombia's international reserves, the foreign money the central bank keeps in hand, at 31 December 2024. Eesti Pank's Annual Report for 2019 says it has been one of the bank's external asset managers since 2017, under an overlay mandate, with no mandate size given; the report writes the name only as the abbreviation GSAM.
n:JPMorgan Asset Management (UK) Limited: JPMorgan Asset Management (UK) Limited, in the United Kingdom, invests money on behalf of clients. Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, hands part of the country's foreign reserves to outside firms to invest actively on its behalf, and its reserves management report names this firm as one of the seven firms holding such a dedicated portfolio at 31 December 2024.
n:Joumhourria Bank: Joumhourria Bank is linked to the Central Bank of Libya through one career record. Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf, at the Central Bank of Libya from 1985 and Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012 and again from 2024, was a member of Joumhourria Bank's supervisory committee from 2012 to 2022.
n:Libyan Financial Services Company: The Libyan Financial Services Company appears here because of one person's career. Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf spent his working life at the Central Bank of Libya, which he joined in 1985, serving as Director of the Governor's Office from 1999 to 2012 and again from 2024. For much of that time, from 2009 to 2024, he was Deputy Chairman of the Libyan Financial Services Company.
n:Libyan Foreign Bank: The Libyan Foreign Bank is tied to the Central Bank of Libya through one career. Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf, who joined the Central Bank of Libya in 1985 and was Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012 and again from 2024, was a member of the Libyan Foreign Bank's supervisory committee from 2007 to 2012.
n:National Bank of Serbia vaults, Belgra: This is the National Bank of Serbia's own vault space in Belgrade, where the bank keeps its gold rather than leaving it with anyone abroad. Its annual report for 2024 sets out the make-up of the foreign exchange reserves at 31 December 2024 as foreign securities at 59.16 percent, money in accounts abroad at 22.04 percent, gold in the bank's vaults at 13.26 percent, and foreign cash and special drawing rights. The whole of the gold holding sits in those vaults. This is storage, not management.
n:Produbanco: Produbanco, formally Banco de la Produccion S.A., is a bank in Ecuador. Juan Diego Mosquera Pesantes has been a director and board member of it since 2014. The curriculum vitae Produbanco publishes for him records that in 1981 he was a delegate and member of the Monetary Board at the Banco Central del Ecuador, and that he had earlier been the founding manager of Citibank Quito and a manager of Banco del Azuay.
UBS Asset Management (Americas) Inc. is an asset manager, meaning a firm that invests money on behalf of clients. Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, hands part of the country's international reserves, the foreign money a central bank keeps in hand, to outside firms to invest actively for it. The bank's reserves management report names this firm as one of seven outside firms each running a dedicated actively managed portfolio of those reserves at 31 December 2024.
n:UBS Asset Management (UK) Ltd: UBS Asset Management (UK) Ltd, at 5 Broadgate in London, invests money on behalf of clients. The Central Bank of Ireland ran a public tender, reference 2022P012, to appoint an investment manager for the bank's own portfolio of shares, and the Irish contract award notice names this firm as the contractor, for a contract valued at 10 million euro excluding value added tax.
n:Wellington Management Company LLP: Wellington Management Company LLP is a firm that invests money for clients. Part of Colombia's international reserves is run this way: the reserves management report of Banco de la Republica, the country's central bank, names Wellington as one of seven outside firms each running a dedicated actively managed portfolio of those reserves at 31 December 2024, which means the firm buys and sells on the central bank's behalf rather than simply holding what it is given.
n:Government of the State of Eritrea: The Government of the State of Eritrea, in Asmara, fills and pays the posts at the Bank of Eritrea, the country's central bank. Proclamation 93/1997, the law that governs the bank, gives the President the appointment of the Governor for a five-year term with the national legislature's approval, the appointment of the Deputy Governor, and the setting of the Governor's pay on the Board's recommendation. The names of all nominated Board members go to the President for appointment, the fee each Board member is paid for a meeting attended is approved by the President, and a director who wishes to resign writes to the President and leaves only when the President accepts the resignation. The same law says the bank is not subject to instructions from the Government over its functions, its budget or its procedures, and the Governor may be relieved only for just cause after the legislature is consulted. The arrangement has no end date.
n:Ministry of Finance of Eritrea: The Ministry of Finance of Eritrea, in Asmara, has a seat on the board of the Bank of Eritrea. Under Article 8 of Proclamation 93/1997 the board is made up of the Governor, the Deputy Governor, a representative of the Ministry of Finance, the Auditor General and three other members. The Ministry nominates its own representative, and that representative is one of the four people who jointly draw up the list of candidates from which the three other members are chosen. A minister of the government may also be asked to take part in board meetings, without a vote.
n:Auditor General of Eritrea: The Auditor General of Eritrea sits on the board of the Bank of Eritrea. Article 8 of Proclamation 93/1997 names the Auditor General as one of the seven board members, alongside the Governor, the Deputy Governor, a representative of the Ministry of Finance and three members drawn from commerce, finance, industry or agriculture. The Auditor General is also one of the four officials who jointly prepare the candidate lists for those three seats. Which firm or body audits the bank's own accounts is not recorded on this map: a 1999 United States government guide says an independent local accounting firm audits it and names no firm.
n:Banco Unión (Paraguay): Banco Union was a private bank in Paraguay that the Central Bank of Paraguay took over and declared bankrupt. On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from Union and the other failed bank, Orienta. Jose Pecci, former superintendent of the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal.
n:Government of Timor-Leste: The Government of Timor-Leste, in Dili, decides what the Banco Central de Timor-Leste does with the country's Petroleum Fund, which the bank manages day to day. Article 11 of the Petroleum Fund Law, Law No. 9/2005 of 3 August as amended by Law No. 12/2011, says the Government is responsible for the overall management of the Fund, and that the Minister of Finance signs a contract with the central bank for its operational management. Article 12(5) requires an investment manager to act within any instructions the Minister issues and within that contract. Ministerial Diploma No. 4/2019 of 1 March 2019 shows the arrangement in use: the Government had decided that the Fund's investments in petroleum operations would be carried out by the state oil company TIMOR GAP, under a contract to be signed by the bank as the Fund's Operational Manager. The arrangement covers the Fund and not the bank's other work.
n:Assembly of the Republic of North Mace: The Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia, in Skopje, is where a bill to take part of the National Bank's money was tabled. In January 2025 a group of its members put forward, under the shortened procedure, amendments to the Law on the National Bank that would send the remainder of the Bank's annual financial result to the state Budget once 30 per cent has gone to general reserves, or 15 per cent after base capital is reached, and that would require the Bank to transfer the special reserves it had already formed, which the bill puts at almost 27 million euros, into general reserves within 30 days and not to use them before then. An amendment to that law was enacted as Sluzben vesnik 16/25 and the Bank's own decisions cite it from 4 February 2025; the enacted text itself has not been read, so what it contains is not confirmed here.
n:Interbank Burundi SA: Interbank Burundi is a commercial bank in Bujumbura. Its own annual report states that the shareholding has been entirely private from the start, held today by Burundians and foreigners, resident and non-resident, of more than ten nationalities, with staff taking part, and it describes itself as one of the pioneers of private banking in Burundi. Mathias Sinamenye, who was Governor of the Bank of the Republic of Burundi from 1992 to 1998, sits on its board: the 2022 annual report lists him as chairman of the audit committee and the 2024 report as chairman of the credit committee.
n:Priorbank: Priorbank is a bank in Belarus, and a report on its sale calls it the largest private bank in the country. The same report says 87.74 per cent of its shares were to be transferred to a buyer named SOVEN 1, that stake having been held until then through a subsidiary of the Austrian group Raiffeisen Bank International. An official who served at the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus from 1998 to 2005, finishing as a deputy head of department, worked at Priorbank from 2005 to 2016 in roles including head of the project management office, chief digital officer and head of retail banking. No source read states the bank's head office city, so it is not placed on the map.
n:Banco Internacional de Moçambique: Banco Internacional de Mocambique, which trades as Millennium bim, is a bank in Mozambique. Its holdings are stated and mixed: 66.69 per cent is held by BCP Internacional II, a subsidiary of a privately owned Portuguese bank, 17.76 per cent by the Mozambican state, 4.95 per cent by the national social security institute, 4.15 per cent by the state insurer EMOSE, 1.08 per cent by a development foundation and 5.37 per cent by managers, technicians and staff. Teotonio Jaime dos Anjos Comiche, who had run the accounting department and then the accounting directorate of the Banco de Mocambique and sat on its board of administration from 1989 to 1992, was an executive director here from 2000 to 2015.
n:Joint Development Bank: Joint Development Bank is a commercial bank in Laos. Its own history page lists Somphao Phaisith among the presidents of its management board from 2007 to 2009, and he became Governor of the Bank of the Lao PDR in 2009. The same page sets out the shareholding for those years: Thai investors held 70 per cent and the Lao side, represented by the Bank of the Lao PDR, held the remaining 30 per cent. On 15 June 2010 the central bank transferred all of its shares to a Thai investor, which the page says left the bank wholly privately owned.
ACLEDA Bank Plc. is a bank based in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, tied to one central bank. It began as an NGO and became a registered bank in 2000, and in that year it took on as chairman of its board Chea Sok, who had spent 1990 to 1999 inside the National Bank of Cambodia as Deputy Governor, Director of the Bank Supervision and Examination Department, Director of the Economic Research Department and General Director. He chaired the board until his retirement, announced by the bank on 16 October 2014. The bank is privately held: its own shareholder table of 20 August 2024 gives AFT 28.0564 per cent, SMBC 18.0669 per cent, public shareholders 17.6828 per cent, COFIBRED and ORIX 12.1271 per cent each, shareholders legalized from ASA Plc. 5.7523 per cent, NHTPE Rumdul 3.5000 per cent, TMF 1.4485 per cent and TFSF 1.2388 per cent, with no government holding.
n:Banco Multiple Promerica de la Republi: Banco Múltiple Promerica de la República Dominicana, S.A. is a bank based in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, tied to one central bank. Its executive president since 2017, Carlos Julio Camilo Vincent, worked in the economic area of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana before joining; the bank's own corporate governance report for 2025 states the central bank post without a title or dates. The same report's shareholder table shows the bank is privately held, with Promerica Financial Corporation holding 89.21 per cent and preferred shareholders 10.79 per cent, and no state body on the register.
n:Promerica Financial Corporation: Promerica Financial Corporation is a firm tied to one central bank. It is the parent of Banco Múltiple Promerica de la República Dominicana, holding 89.21 per cent of its common shares according to the Dominican bank's own corporate governance report for 2025. That holding is what establishes the Dominican bank as privately owned, which is the point on which its executive president's move out of the Banco Central de la República Dominicana counts on this map. No source opened here states the corporation's own head office.
n:Capital Bank Group: Capital Bank Group is a bank based in Amman, Jordan, tied to one central bank. Ayman Omran Abdullah Abu Dahim joined it as chief financial officer in 2011 from the Saudi Central Bank's Banking Institute, where he had been acting head of the Financial and Banking Studies Unit. The National Bank of Iraq's 2024 annual report, which records that career, also gives Jordan Capital Bank 61.85 per cent of the National Bank of Iraq, and states that the bank enjoys no governmental protection or privileges. One qualification is on the record: his own biography says he sat on the Capital Bank board representing Jordan's General Organization for Social Security, a state pension body, so a state fund held shares in it at some point, and no Jordanian share register could be opened.
n:National Bank of Iraq: The National Bank of Iraq is a bank based in Baghdad, Iraq, tied to one central bank. Its chief executive and board member since 15 April 2018 is Ayman Omran Abdullah Abu Dahim, who came out of the Saudi Central Bank's Banking Institute by way of Capital Bank Group in Jordan. The bank's own 2024 annual report gives its ownership as Jordan Capital Bank 61.85 per cent, Cairo Amman Bank 9.9 per cent, Al Bawadi Al Khadra 9.59 per cent and Arcadia LLC 5 per cent, and states that it has no governmental protection or privileges.
n:International Development Bank for Inv: The International Development Bank for Investment and Finance is a bank based in Baghdad, Iraq, tied to one central bank. Its 2017 annual report describes its board member and managing director, Fouad Mohammed Al-Jawahri, as having served as an executive with both the Central Bank of Iraq and Al-Bilad Islamic Bank. The same report, for the same year, states that the Khalaf Abdel Karim family remains the biggest shareholder with 61 per cent of total equity, so the career sentence and the ownership sentence carry no gap between them.
n:BOA Madagascar (Bank of Africa Madagas: BOA Madagascar, the Bank of Africa's Malagasy subsidiary, is a bank based in Antananarivo, Madagascar, tied to one central bank. In November 2014 its own chairman of the board, Alain Hervé Rasolofondraibe, was appointed Governor of the Central Bank of Madagascar; the bank's 2014 annual report states it twice, in the year's calendar and in his successor's letter.
