Its share register at 24 April 2015 gives AFH-Océan Indien 41.26 per cent, the International Finance Corporation 10.40 per cent, FMO 9.45 per cent, Proparco 4.40 per cent, Malagasy private shareholders 24.83 per cent, the Malagasy State 9.37 per cent and others 0.29 per cent, so the State is a minority holder. Five months separate the appointment from the register, which is stated rather than smoothed over.
n:Access Bank (SL) Limited: Access Bank (SL) Limited is a bank based in Freetown, Sierra Leone, tied to one central bank. Its own board page names the non-executive director Ibrahim Khalil Lamin as a former Senior Director of the Financial System Stability Area at the Bank of Sierra Leone and Director of its Financial Markets and Banking departments. The bank's corporate profile describes it as an indirect subsidiary of Access Holdings Plc. Neither the central bank posts nor the board appointment carries a date in the sources read.
n:AFG Bank Comores: AFG Bank Comores is a bank based in Moroni, Comoros, tied to one central bank. Its own comité de direction page says that Al-Habib Sagaf Said Omar, head of Marketing and Customer Experience since 2021, accumulated experience within institutions including the Banque Centrale des Comores. The page gives him no job title and no dates at the central bank, which makes this career sentence thinner than a titled post. The bank is a subsidiary of the Atlantic Group's financial holding, founded by Koné Dossongui; the group's history page records a 1990 structure in which the Comorian State held 34 per cent and does not say that stake was ever sold.
n:Faisal Islamic Bank (Sudan): Faisal Islamic Bank (Sudan) is a bank based in Khartoum, Sudan, tied to one central bank. Abdall Hassan Ahmed was its general manager from 1985 to 1990 and then Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Central Bank of Sudan from 1996 to 1998, a career the central bank itself publishes on its own site. The bank's own pages give its ownership as 11,352 shareholders, 63 per cent individuals and 37 per cent companies, 78 per cent of them non-Sudanese, with 86 private Sudanese and Saudi founders registering it as a public limited company in 1977. The ownership figures are recent and the post was in the 1980s, which is stated rather than hidden.
n:Banco de Guatemala vaults, Guatemala C: The Banco de Guatemala's own reserve vaults in Guatemala City hold one central bank's gold. The bank keeps coined gold worth 2,431.2 million quetzales, 315.5 million US dollars, in those vaults at 31 December 2024, while the remaining 263.1 million dollars of its monetary gold sits abroad. By value, most of the holding is in the bank's own building rather than with a foreign custodian.
n:Banque Centrale de Tunisie vaults, Tun: The Banque Centrale de Tunisie's own vaults in Tunis hold one central bank's gold. Of the bank's 4,135,982 grams of gold bars at 31 December 2023, 2,729,950 grams sit in its own vaults and 1,406,032 grams are placed on term, against total holdings of 6.8 tonnes of fine gold. About two thirds of the bar holding is therefore physically with the bank.
n:MSE Audit Service LLP: MSE Audit Service LLP is an audit firm based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, tied to one central bank. It signed the independent auditor's report on the National Bank of Ethiopia's accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025, in Addis Ababa on 30 December 2025, with Seid Abdela FCCA as engagement partner and an unqualified opinion. Its letterhead reads 'Formerly AW Thomas' and 'Member firm of Grant Thornton International Ltd', and gives its address as the Grant Thornton Building, 4th Floor, Guinea Conakry Street, Kazanchis District. The same report sets out two key audit matters: a net operating loss of 428.56 billion birr and negative equity of 380 billion birr, driven by 445 billion birr of unrealised exchange losses after the change in exchange rate regime and 57.2 billion birr of losses on gold sales and write-downs.
n:Grant Thornton Tunisie: Grant Thornton Tunisie is an audit firm based in Tunis, Tunisia, tied to one central bank. It audits the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, signing the independent auditor's report on the accounts to 31 December 2025 in Tunis on 18 May 2026, with Elmoez Ben Amor as partner and an unqualified opinion; the accounts show a balance sheet total of 131,274,381,414 ouguiya and comprehensive income of 4,048,874,109 ouguiya. The engagement was given by the Mauritanian bank's Conseil Général. Two things follow from the signature. The auditor is not in Mauritania, so the bank's accounts are signed off across a border; and the firm signs as a member of Grant Thornton International, the same network behind the Ethiopian central bank's auditor.
n:Auditeurs Associes CGA: Auditeurs Associés CGA is an audit firm based in Antananarivo, Madagascar, tied to one central bank. It is one half of a joint audit of Banky Foiben'i Madagasikara: its partner Rivoharisoa Randriambelomanana signed the Rapport des auditeurs externes on the accounts to 31 December 2025 alongside Julien Koscien of Deloitte & Associés, the report dated in Antananarivo and Paris-La Défense together on 29 April 2026. Its address is Immeuble Les Jardins de Mahamasina, 101 Antananarivo. One of the report's key audit matters is the valuation of staff retirement and seniority benefits under the revised IAS 19, where the bank's social commitments stood at 267.5 billion ariary at 31 December 2025 against 305.7 billion a year earlier.
BDO & Associados, SROC, S.A. is an audit firm based in Lisbon, Portugal, tied to one central bank. It audits the Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe, and its report on the accounts to 31 December 2024, published by the bank on 13 February 2026, carries a QUALIFIED opinion, which is unusual for a central bank. Four matters sit behind the qualification. The bank's assets include 1,517,669,216 dobras claimed against the State, among them 388,323,250 dobras of interest-free emergency credit granted in 2022 after the floods of late 2021, a 73,500,000 dobra advance in 2024 for fuel imports, 28,169,592 dobras of pre-2000 credits whose contracts provide for interest that has never been recorded, and 657,177,194 dobras owed by the Banco Nacional de Angola under a 1988 banking agreement the State later used in a settlement with Angola; the auditor says the first two did not meet article 26 of the bank's Organic Law, which capped State borrowing at 5 per cent of the previous year's tax revenue and required settlement within the year. A 2022 transfer of 419,911,000 dobras of construction in progress for the bank's new head office included about 34,674,000 dobras advanced to a contractor whose contract the bank terminated in 2017 for non-performance. The bank's 61.1 per cent holding in the payments company SPAUT is carried at 33,491,704 dobras while SPAUT's own equity had fallen to 3,756,626 dobras. And 43,192,500 dobras remain receivable from Energy Bank STP, whose licence the central bank cancelled in January 2022. The auditor concludes that assets and equity are overstated. The firm's own footer describes it as a Portuguese company and a member of BDO International Limited.
n:Banque de Montréal (Bank of Montreal): The Banque de Montréal, Bank of Montreal, is a bank based in Montreal, Canada, tied to one central bank. It holds the larger part of Haiti's gold: the Banque de la République d'Haïti's audited statements to 30 September 2023 put 56,905.49 troy ounces on deposit with it, at a fair value of 14,290,663 thousand gourdes against a cost of 4,254,700 thousand. That is all but 1,307.53 ounces of the bank's 58,213.02-ounce holding. The same note records that these reserves earn no interest.
n:Federal Reserve Bank: This node is a Federal Reserve Bank that one central bank's accounts do not identify further. The Banque de la République d'Haïti's audited statements to 30 September 2023 put 1,307.53 troy ounces of its gold on deposit at 'la Federal Reserve Bank', with a fair value of 328,360 thousand gourdes, and name no particular Reserve Bank and no city. This map carries a separate node for the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, which other banks' documents name explicitly, and the two are kept apart on purpose: naming New York here would be an inference rather than something Haiti's statements say.
n:AFFINOR: AFFINOR is a firm tied to one central bank, holding gold for the Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée. KPMG's audit of the bank's IFRS statements at 31 December 2023 puts 100,950.47 ounces of its monetary gold with AFFINOR, the largest of the four holdings named in that note. The same note records that a gold-processing contractor holding 3.1 tonnes, which is the same 100,950.47 ounces, had failed to return the deposit since January 2022; the bank won an arbitration award at the ICC in Paris in September 2024 and carries a provision of 888.51 billion Guinean francs, half the fair value, against the holding. The audit opinion carries an emphasis-of-matter paragraph on it. The note gives no address for the firm.
n:BRINKS: BRINKS is a firm tied to one central bank, holding gold for the Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée. KPMG's audit of the bank's IFRS statements at 31 December 2023 puts 47,425.02 ounces of its monetary gold with BRINKS, priced at 2,062.4 US dollars an ounce. The note names four holders in all, BRI, AFFINOR, BRINKS and EMR, and gives no address or country for any of the three commercial handlers.
n:EMR: EMR is a firm tied to one central bank, holding gold for the Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée. n:Central Vault of the National Bank of: The Central Vault of the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus, in Minsk, holds one central bank's gold. The National Bank's own gold reserve statistics page states that the gold reserve values are stored in the Central Vault of the National Bank, and that the gold forms part of the State Fund of Precious Metals and Precious Stones of the Republic of Belarus, which the National Bank administers. The same page adds that some holdings are also placed on accounts and deposits abroad, and names none of those institutions.
n:Presidential palace vault, Kabul: The vault at the presidential palace in Kabul held part of one central bank's gold. A Reuters report of 18 August 2021, reading Da Afghanistan Bank's own financial statement, put just under 160 million US dollars of the Afghan central bank's gold bars and silver coins there; the figure covers gold and silver together, so the gold share alone is not given. The Taliban took control of the palace in August 2021. The rest of the bank's gold sits at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, which held bars worth 101,770,256,000 afghanis, about 1.32 billion US dollars, at the end of 2020.
n:Aviva Investors Global Services Limite: Aviva Investors Global Services Limited is a firm based in London, United Kingdom, tied to one central bank. The National Bank of Kazakhstan's consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2012 name it as one of six foreign asset management organisations to which the bank transferred part of its international reserves that year, with 47,411,430 thousand tenge under its management on a global developing markets strategy against the ML Emerging Customised Index. That is a 2012 position: the bank's 2018 and 2024 reports say external managers are used and name none, so no source says this mandate still runs.

n:Lombard Odier Asset Management (Europe: Lombard Odier Asset Management (Europe) Limited is a firm tied to one central bank. n:Korea Investment Corporation: The Korea Investment Corporation is a firm based in Seoul, South Korea, tied to one central bank. Its Santiago Principles self-assessment, published by the International Forum of Sovereign Wealth Funds, says under Principle 4 that it manages assets entrusted by the government, the Bank of Korea and other public funds defined under the National Finance Act, citing articles of the KIC Act. The limits of that sentence are worth stating: it never calls those assets foreign exchange reserves, gives no amount for the Bank of Korea portion and gives no date, and the Bank of Korea's own reserve management page could not be opened.
n:Informed Portfolio Management: Informed Portfolio Management is a Swedish asset manager in Stockholm, tied to one central bank. Eesti Pank's Annual Report for 2019 says the firm has worked for it since 2007, as one of four external asset managers running what the report calls overlay mandates, in which the managers express most strategies through derivative instruments rather than by buying the assets outright. The report gives no mandate size and no share of the reserves, and the position it describes is as at 31 December 2019. Its registered office at Mäster Samuelsgatan 6 in Stockholm comes from the United Kingdom company register, which records it as an overseas company incorporated in Sweden; the Estonian report gives no address.
